articleTitle: DC Microgrid for Renewable Applications Taking Into Account the Load Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In today's engineering world, with the advancement of renewable resources, microgrids have received much attention. In this paper, in order to increase the number of distributed generation modules, a system consisting of three distributed generations considering dynamic loads is studied. Instead of a simple resistor, a boost DC-DC converter is considered for the load. A passivity control with a droop voltage control approach controls the entire system's stability. The simulation of the system, along with its controllers, is performed through the Simulink platform in MATLAB software. Several different scenarios are taken into account to obtain the presented results.

articleTitle: Enhancing Photovoltaic System Performance Through Particle Swarm Optimization with Time-Varying Acceleration Coefficients (TVAC-PSO) for MPPT in Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Finding the maximum power point might be a challenging task and even more when the solar panels are partially shaded, and this is due to the nonlinearity of the PV panel characteristics curves. This nonlinearity induces the traditional maximum power tracking methods, such as P&O and incremental conductance, in the wrong way leading them to a premature convergence to the wrong solution. One of the most popular algorithm used to overcome this drawback, is the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. However, this algorithm is characterized by a relatively long convergence time. In this study we will demonstrate the advantages of using Time-Varying Acceleration Coefficients Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm (TVAC-PSO) over the conventional PSO. By using variable parameters, TVAC-PSO enhances the power production of the PV array in partially shaded conditions and converges to the optimal solution considerably faster. The effectiveness of the algorithm is verified with the obtained numerical simulation results using Matlab Simulink.

articleTitle: Comparative Experimental Study of Voltage Waveform Influences on Ozone Production Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The use of DBD reactors for ozone production has been prevalent for decades, and numerous studies have been conducted since the emergence of this reactor type, aiming to enhance the production process and energy efficiency, This study investigates how different voltage shapes (triangular, rectangular, and sinusoidal) affect a cylindrical ozone generator with a DBD reactor. The system's efficacy is determined by calculating the ozone concentration produced and analyzing its energy efficiency., The applied voltage(0-9kv) and frequency(100 - 1,1khz) were taken as control factors in the study, The results obtained have demonstrated the superiority of the triangular voltage waveform in terms of ozone production and energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Hybrid Beamforming Design Based on Low Complexity Alternating Minimizing Solution for Millimeter Wave MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) bands have deservedly taken their place in the development of next-generation network communications to address the explosive growth of mobile network data traffic and high-speed communications requirements. Also, the fully connected hybrid architecture can offer a suitable beamforming gain for overcoming the limitations of mm Wave signals in outdoor communications. Consequently, for the feasibility of the hybrid architecture implementation, the designing of the optimal analog/digital beamformers is indispensable for providing good performance with the lowest complexity. Therefore, in this work, we develop a low-complexity alternating minimization design using a complete closed-form least-square method in the iterative design process to derive the optimal analog and digital beamformers by considering the total power constraint at the transmitter and the unit constant modulus constraints. Thanks to the offered global optimal solutions and the fast convergence of the least squares method, numerical results demonstrated that the proposed design attains perfect performance with the lowest computational complexity compared to the state-of-art design algorithms in terms of spectral efficiency (SE) in different scenarios.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of a CPW-Fed UWB Antenna for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper investigates a compact coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna for use in breast cancer detection. By integrating a pair of T-shaped slots into the ground plane, a bandwidth enhancement is accomplished. Measurement demonstrated the UWB performance of the suggested antenna. Moreover, variations in specific absorption rate (SAR) values are observed between two different scenarios, with and without the presence of a tumor. The presented antenna, having a compact size of 20x28 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, is suitable to be employed in microwave imaging applications.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation to Bearing-Fault Signatures in Defective Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This article presents, through an experimental study, the relative indicators of the bearing fault in induction motors on the basis of different signals. In addition to proposed bearing fault signatures in the literature, new signatures presented in our paper are investigated. These new signals show that the predictability of bearing failures can be improved, compared to vibration signals which required access to the machine body.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Impact of Attention Mechanisms on UNet and Res-UNet Models for Building Extraction Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Accurate extraction of building footprints from remote sensing imagery is essential for various applications, including change detection, automatic mapping, urban planning, and 3D reconstruction. However, the intricate nature of building structures and their surroundings in satellite imagery poses unique challenges for extraction, such as diverse building appearances and complex ground backgrounds. Despite advancements in machine learning algorithms, achieving precise extraction remains a persistent challenge. Semantic segmentation using deep learning, particularly the UNet architecture, has emerged as a promising approach for building extraction in satellite imagery. This paper aims to enhance the accuracy of building footprint extraction by integrating attention mechanisms. Specifically, our work focuses on applying attention mechanisms to the UNet architecture. The objective of this research is to assess the efficiency of attention mechanisms. This is achieved by contrasting the performance outcomes of four distinct models: UNet, Attention UNet, Res-UNet, and Attention Res-UNet. Through systematic assessment of the impact of attention mechanisms on each architecture, we aim to identify the most effective approach for improving building extraction accuracy in satellite imagery.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis: An Integrated Methodology Based on Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The main objective of this research is to propose an effective fault diagnosis method for systems. Detecting faults early prevents system failure and even disasters with severe consequences for individuals and materials. In this paper, the use of neural networks for detecting and isolating faults of an egg incubator system is applied. The results illustrate the effective detection and isolation of faults achieved with this method.

articleTitle: Surface Disinfection in Hospital Environment and Public Transport Using Gaseous Ozone in Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Like other countries, Algeria has suffered a lot during the covid-19 pandemic. This work is aimed to a case study of surface disinfection in hospital environment and public transport to convince the political authorities the efficiency of ozone disinfection. In this paper, the disinfection capacity using ozone gas was studied by analysing the reduction of bacteria colonies inside an ablution room in the forensic medicine service of the university hospital centre and inside a tramway of Sidi-Bel-Abbes city. An experimental study was performed to determine the capacities of ozone disinfection in different surfaces by analysing E.coli and total flora. The microbiological analysis before and after treatment pointed out that a high disinfection efficiency with rates well above 80% were obtained for an operating time between 60 and 120 minutes.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effect of Flow Path Geometry on PEMFC Performance and Reactant Distribution Using CFD Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The objectif of this study is to evaluate the impact of the flow field geometry within the bipolar plate channels on the performance of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFC). To achieve this goal, a three-dimensional, isothermal, and steady-state computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model was developed for a 25-flow channel fuel cell, incorporating a mix of serpentine, vertical parallel, and horizontal parallel configurations. The equations are solved numerically using the ANSYS Fluent code. The focus was on analyzing the polarization curve and reactant distribution, specifically examining water vapor distribution, as well as oxygen and hydrogen profiles at the cathode and anode, respectively, for different voltages. The findings demonstrated a 20% improvement in cell performance when using the suggested mixed geometry, as opposed to the parallel configuration. Additionally, the knowledge derived from analyzing the water vapor, oxygen, and hydrogen profiles has enriched our understanding of the intricate phenomena associated with the geometry, shedding light on how these factors affect reactant distribution within the PEMFC and, consequently, shape its overall performance.

articleTitle: Estimation of Frequency-Selective MIMO Channels Using DDST and ZCZ Sequences
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Data Dependent Superimposed Training (DDST) was proposed as an improvement of Superimposed Training (ST) channel estimation scheme. The idea is to cancel the effect of information data on the ST performance by superimposing an additional sequence. This paper is devoted to the study of the channel estimation performance of Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) based on DDST method. First, we propose a new approach that allows obtaining a closed-form expression for the variance of the estimation error. Second, the precise correlation properties of the training sequences are extracted. Indeed, it is shown that the training sequences must have a zero correlation zone in their autocorrelation and cross-correlation functions. Consequently, optimal and interference-free estimation performance is obtained when the channel length is lower than the zero zone length.

articleTitle: APSO-Enhanced Optimization of NFTSMC and HGO for a Photovoltaic Pumping System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this research, a robust control based on a software sensor is developed to optimize the performance of a photovoltaic pumping system (PVPS). The system architecture includes a photovoltaic generator (PVG) connected to a Permanent Mag-net DC Motor (PMDC), which operates a centrifugal pump through a DC-DC boost converter. The regulation of the boost converter's duty cycle is achieved using a non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control (NFTSMC) approach. To lower the overall cost of the PVPS, a high-gain observer (HGO) is implemented. The Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization (APSO) algorithm is employed to fine-tune the control gains. The proposed control strategy's effectiveness is demonstrated through comprehensive simulations under varying atmospheric conditions using Matlab/Simulink. Comparative analysis with a sliding mode controller based on HGO reveals that the proposed method ensures rapid and accurate tracking of the maximum power point, as well as strong robustness against disturbances and uncertainties.

Author Keywords: Non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control

articleTitle: Short-Circuit Protection of IGBTs Using Collector-Emitter Current Slope Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Insulated-gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) are crucial components in power electronics, capable of handling high voltages and currents efficiently. However, short-circuit faults pose a significant risk, potentially leading to catastrophic device failure. This paper proposes a novel short-circuit protection method for IGBTs that monitors the rapid change in collectoremitter current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\frac{di}{dt})$</tex> during a fault. By detecting the surge in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{di}{dt}$</tex>, the proposed technique enables faster fault detection and response compared to conventional methods, enhancing IGBT reliability and lifespan. Comprehensive analysis and experimental results validate the effectiveness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{di}{dt}$</tex> monitoring in mitigating short-circuit stress, extending IGBT lifetime, and ultimately improving system robustness.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Thermal Conductive Materials for Optimizing the Thermal Management of a Lithium-Ion Battery Pack
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The temperature of the battery significantly influences the safety and performance of lithium-ion batteries. Optimal efficiency and safety are achieved within a temperature range of 20°C to 40°C. This range can be maintained by limiting the supplied current or, more commonly, by improving the cooling system to enhance heat dissipation. Battery management systems are designed to prevent thermal runaway of the cells. The choice of an effective thermal conductor for heat dissipation is crucial, particularly if the system lacks other means of cooling, such as external fluid circulation, typically air. This document presents a comparison of different materials used to improve the cooling of a pack consisting of multiple lithium-ion cells, providing a nominal voltage of 12V. The cell pack is either submerged or directly covered with a thermal conductor. As a reference, air is chosen as the first material, followed by two conventional materials, paraffin and silicon carbide, and then a polymer positioned between these two materials. Additionally, two recently developed liquids for this application, AC-100 and Novec-7000, are tested. Paraffin and AC-100 demonstrate superior performance with a 10°C variance compared to air. Nonetheless, paraffin falls short of reaching its melting point. The paraffin-silicone polymer combination yields outcomes comparable to paraffin. While for the Novec 7000 we obtain the best results in terms of performance with a peak cell temperature of 38°C. The cells are subjected to their maximum operating current, and temperature images are provided, along with a comparison of the pack voltage based on the material used.

articleTitle: Development of an Optical System for Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Several people must frequently evaluate their blood glucose since it is an important indicator of health problems mainly Diabetes. Different medical systems are commercialized to measure blood glucose levels; some are invasive others are noninvasive. The main purpose of this article is to develop a non-invasive device for measuring blood glucose levels based on the detection and analysis of the Photoplethysmogram signal. The developed systems include an optical sensor to detect the PPG signal, digitalizing and acquiring boards to a computer and a software program to process and analyze the digitalized PPG signal regarding some features extracted from its waveform. These features are the systolic amplitude Sa and the b/a amplitude ratio in the second derivative PPG (SDPPG) waveform. An invasive glucometer is also used along with the Sa and b/a ratio determined from the developed system to generate a calibration model which is used to deduce BGL values. The result showed that the calibration model using the b/a ratio is more accurate for non-invasive blood level measurement then that of Sa with a difference in glucose estimation around 2mg/dl and with the correlation coefficient (R2) of the glucose level prediction between 0.8904 and 0.9775.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Behavior of a Standalone PV System Based on Classical and Advanced MPPT Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Over the last few years, several control methods for Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) of Photovoltaic (PV) systems have been developed to ensure that the solar cells operate at their maximum power point under varying conditions as the temperature and irradiance change. The work of this paper is dedicated to a comprehensive comparative analysis of both classical: Incremental Conductance (InC), Perturb and Observe (P&O), Hill climbing (HC), and advanced: Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) MPPT algorithms, all of them have been created for PV system and simulated to obtain the various system responses such as the power and the voltage on Direct Current (DC) load. The results of the simulation tests confirmed that the algorithm based on ANN has the fastest response time; the respective stability percentages of HC, FLC, ANN, P&O, InC, and PSO were found to be 76%, 88.9%, 96.9%, 97.03%, 97.05%, and 97.5%.

articleTitle: Multi Objective Optimal Design for Multi-State Power System Using the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study addresses the problem of optimal design for series-parallel multi-state power systems, where each system component is available in the market in several versions. The Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is applied to determine the optimal system structure or the optimal combination of versions for each subsystem or component. A two-objective problem is first considered, where the aim is to maximize system reliability while minimizing the investment cost. The second problem has three objective functions and is defined to maximize reliability and performance while minimizing the investment cost. The results show that NSGA-II can provide better solutions than another recently proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Investigating Deep Saturation Effects in Buck Converters Through Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Deep saturation in buck converters can significantly degrade performance and lead to component failure. A primary cause of this issue is improper inductor core selection. This paper proposes a data-driven modeling approach to capture the non-linear relationship between inductor current and inductance. By incorporating this non-linear model, we can analyze the effects of saturation through simulations and experiments. Our approach facilitates the evaluation of trade-offs between utilizing a smaller, potentially more saturation-prone inductor versus a larger inductor with increased size and cost.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control For Underactuated Nonlinear Mechanical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The Rotary Inverted Pendulum (RIP) serves as a quintessential benchmark in control theory, representing a challenging and unstable system of paramount importance. In this study, we focus on a Quanser platform to investigate the application and significance of sliding mode control in stabilizing the RIP. The importance of RIP lies in its portrayal of real-world control challenges encountered in industries ranging from manufacturing to robotics. Its inherent instability and underactuation make it an ideal testbed for advanced control strategies. Our research delves into the experimental application of sliding mode control, on the Quanser RIP platform. Through rigorous modeling, simulation, and practical implementation, we aim to demonstrate the effectiveness of this control strategy. This study contributes to the broader discourse on control systems and automation, showcasing the potential of sliding mode control in addressing complex and dynamic systems. The outcomes of our research not only advance the understanding of control theory but also have practical implications for industries where precise control and stabilization are critical.

articleTitle: Modified MFP-Unet for Left Ventricle Segmentation from 2D Echocardiographic Images
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Cardiac ultrasound (echocardiography) is a non- invasive medical imaging technique of primordial importance for assessing cardiac function, particularly that of the left ventricle cavity. The delineation of this chamber from 2D echocar- diographic images is essential for diagnosing and monitoring various cardiac pathologies. In this paper, we propose a new deep learning model based on the MFP-Unet architecture for segmentation of the left ventricle from 2D echocardiographic images. The proposed method is a modified MFP-Unet where the main changes are applied to enforce the feature representation of the encoder part. Squeeze and excitation units are added to the skip connections, and a multi-scale input is used to form a pyramid of the same input image. We evaluate the performance of the proposed architecture on the large publicly available Echonet-Dynamic dataset. A Dice similarity coefficient of 0.926, intersection over union of 0.862, Hausdorff distance of 3.96, and an average surface distance of 0.15 are achieved. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of the suggested model and its prospective use in the clinical field.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Electrostatic Separation Techniques Used in the Sorting of WEEE
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study thoroughly analyzes the performance of roll-type electrostatic separators compared to an innovative method based on electrostatically assisted aspiration for sorting copper and PVC particles from electrical cable waste. The results of this study highlight the capacity of roll-type separators to recover between 98 and 100% of PVC particles at relatively low rotation speeds. However, at these speeds, a significant proportion of copper ends up inadvertently in the PVC bins. The new electrostatic separator, on the other hand, offers greater flexibility. By carefully adjusting the parameters, it achieves satisfactory recovery rates for both copper and PVC. Thus, the choice of the most suitable parameters will depend on the desired material and the compromises acceptable in terms of recovery efficiency.

articleTitle: Improvement of Germination and Seedling Growth of Durum Wheat Seed Using Surface Dielectric Barrier Discharge Plasma
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this work, the effect of treating durum wheat with cold plasma created in air at atmospheric pressure without any other gases was investigated. The plasma was created in a Plexiglas chamber using a surface DBD (SDBD) reactor with a hexagonal pattern and a homemade generator providing a pseudo-sinusoidal signal of 9.5kV with a frequency of 2.75 kHz and a duty cycle of 49%. The results obtained showed that the treatment of durum wheat seeds by this device using only air caused improvements both in the germination of the seeds and in the growth of the plants.

articleTitle: A New Optimization Approach to Solve the Optimal Reactive Power Dispatch Problem for Real Power Loss Minimization, Voltage Deviation Minimization and Voltage Stability Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study proposes a novel method based on K-means and the Logistic Chaotic JAYA algorithm (LCJAYA) to resolve the ORPD problem for real power loss minimization, voltage deviation minimization and voltage stability enhancement. Firstly, the K-means method is introduced to cluster the setting of control variables including the generation voltage magnitude, the tap changing transformers and the reactive power of the compensation devices. Then, the LCJAYA is used to determine the cluster centers. The proposed algorithm uses at first, a Logistic Chaotic to enhance the population diversity and to improve the exploration search areas. Then, a chaotic mutation strategy to improve the exploration and the exploitation. IEEE 57 Bus system is used to validate the proposed algorithm. The optimization algorithm is general and can be used to solve other power system optimization problems

articleTitle: Contaminated Transformer Oil Electrification Behaviour
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the behavior of electrostatic charging tendency in contaminated transformer oils. Three types of pollution are considered: Kraft paper particles, copper particles and the mixture of both. The experiments carried out under ambient conditions involve the measurement of electrification currents in previously contaminated transformer oil samples at different rotating velocities of an introduced spinning disc. The disc speeds are adjusted to 80 and 95 revolutions per minute (tr/mn), and the contaminant particle content is set to 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5 grams in a liquid volume of 300ml. The obtained results indicate a significant electrical effect concerning the contamination content and, obviously, the liquid dynamics. The introduction of Kraft paper particles results in fully negative electrification of the transformer oil, while the presence of copper particles tends to reverse the electrification current to a positive sign. The influence of the liquid's dynamics is highlighted differently depending on the type of pollution studied. In fact, the electrification currents tend to decrease with the increase of the liquid speed for single contamination types (paper or copper), while the electrification currents significantly increase with the liquid's dynamics when combined pollution is introduced into the transformer oil.

articleTitle: Improved Direct Power Control of PV-SAPF System using ADALINE and ANN-MPPT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study aims to apply an improved direct power control (DPC) to the Shunt active power filter SAPF using a table of switching, which has to maximize the system performances and minimize the switching number and the current source's total harmonic distortion (THD). AnADALINE controller based on a least mean square (LMS) with an adaptive learning rate is proposed to act on the DC link. SAPF is associated with a PV system. Under variable climate variations, the proposed solution to maximize the power extraction is combining a feedforward artificial neural network (ANN) associated with an ADALINE controller applied to the maximum power point tracking technique (MPPT). For the DC link voltage, a proportional-integral (PI) controller is used. MPPT configurations have been proposed: perturb and observe (P&O), backstepping, integral backstepping based on incremental conductance INC, and fuzzy logic controller (FLC) for the comparative study. The overall system has been evaluated in a MATLAB/Simulink environment. The simulation results confirm the proposed intelligent controls' outperformance, robustness, and effectiveness. The results found that PV power efficacy was around 99%; moreover, DC bus voltage had a settling time of 0.035 seconds, and THD current was 0.94% An experimental application will be proposed to validate the effectiveness of these approaches.

articleTitle: Modified Vivaldi Antenna for Through Wall Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: One of the main objectives of electronics manufacturers is to reduce the weight and size of antennas for integration into electronic systems, particularly portable devices. This article presents an ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna for through-the-wall microwave imaging (TWMI) applications. The aim is to improve antenna performance by modifying a Vivaldi antenna with slots in the conventional structure. Return loss remains below 10 dB, and the radiation pattern remains relatively constant over the entire UWB range (0.8 - 4.5 GHz). The rectangular slots added to the conventional Vivaldi antenna enable an average azimuth gain of around 6 dBi to be achieved. The proposed antenna has been shown to be an especially good candidate for TWMI applications.

articleTitle: Real Time Implementation of a Speed/Torque Sensorless Observer for Induction Motor Utilizing Extended Kalman Filtering Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Sensorless induction motor (IM) drives eliminate the problems encountered with physical sensors such as the complexity of the installation, cost, and accuracy of the measurements. This paper presents the design and real-time implementation of speed and torque observers for IMs. The observer is based on the extended Kalman filter (EKF) known for its ability to handle nonlinear systems and noise. The aim is to accurately predict the crucial operational point of IMs without direct measurement. The paper discusses the theoretical framework of the EKF, detailing its real-time implementation for induction motor control. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed EKF-based speed/torque observer as a viable alternative to traditional speed/torque sensors. Consequently, the proposed solution brings tangible benefits such as reducing the drive system's size, enhanced system reliability, improved motor efficiency and reduced costs.

articleTitle: Improving Load Profile Through Optimal Load Scheduling Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative methodology based on a Genetic Algorithm (GA) to optimize Demand-Side Management (DSM) in the energy domain. The proposed approach utilizes a GA to analyze appliance consumption profiles and identify load shifting opportunities for controllable appliances from peak hours to off-peak hours, defined by Demand Response (DR) programs such as Time-of-Use (TOU) pricing. This optimization enables the reduction of electricity consumption during peak hours, lowers consumer bills, and improves the efficiency of the power grid, contributing to more sustainable and economical energy management.

articleTitle: Characterization of Two Samples (Fe Si GO and Fe Si NGO) Using the Measurement Device
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The characterization of magnetic materials is performed using measurement devices that differ depending on the direction of magnetic induction. A single-strip frame or an Epstein frame are used for magnetic induction in the uniaxial direction. Two samples (Fe Si Go and Fe Si NGo) were characterized in this work using measurement devices. Losses play an important role in electrical engineering design. We will explore loss prediction and contribute to the automation of measurement stations to achieve this goal. articleTitle: HW/SW Co-Design of the Secure Hash Function SHA-256
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Technological developments in data communication has increased the integration cryptographic algorithms. Hash functions are used in many security schemes such as digital signature/verification and block chain network. Secure Hash Algorithm-256 (SHA-256) is an irreversible hash function. Its algorithm is not only fast, but also provides a high security service. However, in terms of computations complexity, it requires a huge amount of arithmetic operations. This paper presents the implementation of SHA-256 core in reconfigurable FPGA circuit. Our work is based on Programmable System on Chip (PSoC) architecture. The Xilinx Microblaze processor is used for the system flexibility. The SHA-256 algorithm is composed by two steps, namely, the padding operation and the hash computation process to produce the 256-bit message digest. The proposed Hardware/Software (HW /SW) partitioning consists in the execution of the padding step in SW whereas the hash computation is implemented in HW within the SHA-256 core. The implementation results on Virtex-5 circuit show that a 512-bit message digest runs in 2.083 us. The PSoC hardware architecture requires 4058 Slices.

articleTitle: Model for Predicting Electrical Energy Consumption in Smart Home with Weather Information
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Energy consumption is increasing every day, which results in ever-increasing energy costs. Developing efficient energy management systems for smart homes by predicting future energy consumption has become a key necessity for many research efforts dealing with energy consumption. Artificial intelligence has demonstrated significant results in the field of management systems. In this paper, we propose three models based on artificial neural network ANN to predict the consumption of each charge. These loads are the main consumers in smart homes. The models are tested against a real database containing disaggregated energy consumption data for specific weather factors. The resulting predictive model enables proactive and effective load control. They are evaluated using performance metrics, including absolute error. The model successfully reproduced consumption curves with an average accuracy of 98%.

articleTitle: System-On-Chip Implementation Of Blind Spectrum Sensing Method Using Discrete Transforms and Hardware/Software Co-Design
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper proposes the application of discrete transforms for unknown signal detection without prior knowledge of their parameters in a blind spectrum sensing context to reliably perform the first and most crucial function of cognitive radio systems. The proposed method is based on the combination of two discrete transforms aimed to improve the detection performance and reduce the detection time, as well as the hardware implementation resource consumption. Firstly, the primary focus of the proposed method is to overcome the problem of noise uncertainty encountered in conventional energy detection method. Secondly, the proposed Hardware/Software implementation enables a considerable reduction in detection time with a modest consumption of hardware resources. Lastly, the proposed Hardware/Software Co-design is experimentally validated by real-time detection of real-world signals using a System-On-Chip that integrates an ARM-based processing unit and an FPGA circuit for hardware implementation. The obtained simulation and implementation results confirm the relevance of the proposed method for embedded cognitive radio systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing Residential Energy Autonomy: Hydrogen Integration with Photovoltaic and Battery Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study, conducted in Tiaret, Algeria, examines the integration of hydrogen technology with solar panels (PV) and batteries to improve residential energy independence. The process involves using surplus electricity from the solar panels for electrolysis, producing hydrogen that is stored for later use, thus reducing reliance on the electrical grid. HOMER Pro was employed to optimize the system setup, and the analysis recommended a configuration consisting of a 5.04 kW solar power system, a 1.5 kW fuel cell, and 40 kWh of battery storage for the location studied. The system was capable of producing 7,702 kWh annually, with 99.7% of the energy coming from PV and 0.3% from fuel cells. This integrated energy management system effectively handles energy surpluses and deficits through a combination of battery storage and hydrogen production. By combining solar power, hydrogen technology, and intelligent energy management, this approach offers a viable path for homes to increase energy self-sufficiency, reduce carbon footprints, and meet rising energy demands while contributing to a more sustainable future.

articleTitle: 10-Element Yagi Antenna for 38 GHz Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this paper, our primary emphasis is on investigating the Yagi antenna at a working frequency of 38 GHz, and evaluate antenna characteristics such as return loss, gain, directivity and radiation pattern. The material for making the antenna consists of PEC pipes as reflector element, driven element and director elements with a diameter of 0.2 mm. The design of the Yagi antenna uses CST studio suite 2021 software. The proposed antenna has return loss values of -16.29 dB, and attains a peak gain of 10.88 dBi for 38 GHz millimeter wave-band. The proposed antenna's performance in terms of radiation efficiency, directivity, gain, and radiation pattern positions it as a viable option for 5G millimeter-wave communication.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Detection Using Aperture Coupled Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The study introduces a simple technique for mammary cancer early detection. The technique is based on a high-performance aperture-coupled patch antenna designed for ISM-band applications, operating at 2.45 GHz with unidirectional radiation and a gain of approximately 6.27 dBi. Rigorous testing involving calculating the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) of the antenna when exposed to the breast tissues, both with and without tumors, yielded highly encouraging results, affirming the antenna's potential for tumor detection. When a tumor is present, there is a substantial increase in SAR values. Particularly, for a tumor with a 20 mm radius, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SAR_{10g}$</tex> increased from 0.96 W/kg to 3.44 W/kg, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SAR_{1g}$</tex> rose from 2.26 W/kg to 6.23 W/kg. These findings contribute to the development of non-invasive and potentially life-saving medical technologies, leveraging advanced antenna designs.

articleTitle: Improved Control of DC Motor Using Parallel Multicellular Converter and Intelligent Control Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper investigates the velocity regulation of a separately excited direct current machine powered by a parallel multicellular step-down converter. The objective is to design a controller that enables the DC motor to track a specified velocity while maintaining optimal performance. To achieve this goal, two feedback mechanisms are implemented-one for current control and a second for velocity regulation. The proposed controllers employed in this study are a Fuzzy Logic controller (FLC) and a Sliding Mode controller (SMC). These controllers are then tested under speed and load torque variations to confirm their efficacy. The SM controller maintains excellent velocity direction tracking even when confronted with external perturbations, and it outperforms the FL controller by a significant margin.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Separation Process for Metal/Plastic Particles by Double-Sided Electric Curtain Conveyor
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This work describes the design of a two-phase, double-sided travelling-wave conveyor, mounted on an electromagnetic vibrator for the separation of a mixture of metal/plastic particles, and powered by a mid-point transformer which delivers two sinusoidal voltages <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$180^{\circ}$</tex> out of phase. An experimental study was carried out to investigate the influence of several factors on the separation of this mixture. The results obtained using a granular “bronze-plastic” mixture show that, depending on the amplitude of the voltages applied, the material flow rate and the inclination of the plane on which the conveyor is positioned: i) plastic particles can move under the effect of vibration; ii) metal particles adhere to the conveyor surface by the force of attraction exerted by the conveyor; iii) separation of a “bronze-plastic” mixture is possible.

articleTitle: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Diabetes Patients: An LSTM-Based Predictive Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Managing blood glucose levels is critically essential in the care of individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), through appropriate medication, physical activities, and continuous glucose monitoring(CGM). The development of wearable technologies has emerged to monitor glucose continuously and administer insulin when necessary, allowing patients to tracktheir glucose levels easily, with swift intervention, and avoiding hospitalization. This work explores a novel deep-learning model to predict future blood glucose levels at different prediction horizons 5, 15, 30, and 60 minutes. We've proposed a bloodglucose prediction systems based on Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and we compare its performance to a baseline model (Simple Recurrent Neural Network).Our experimental results on D1NAMO dataset containing CGM data showed that the proposed LSTM model leads to improved blood glucose prediction accuracy measures compared to the baseline model.

articleTitle: Combined-Fault Detection and Diagnosis in Induction Motor Using Motor Current Signature Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The importance of ensuring the availability and operational safety of electrical machines requires us to develop detection systems that can be capable to supervise and diagnose the health of the systems. The search of fault residuals is primarily aimed at characterizing the operation of the system by identifying the type and origin of the fault. In order to assign a relevant, unambiguous indicator to a specific fault, it is necessary to differentiate between faults or anomalies that may occur at different levels of the process. The main purpose of the presented paper is to visualize the changes and variations in electrical and mechanical quantities when the machine is affected by broken rotor bar faults in presence of unbalanced supply voltage conditions. The proposed method is based primarily on signal spectral analysis of stator current through Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). It is enabling to define the residuals specific to the studying fault. The main objective of the broken rotor bar fault study under unbalanced supply voltage conditions is to conclusively identify the appropriate fault indicator. Both simulation and experimental results supported this hypothesis.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Breakdown Voltage in Air as a Function of Temperature and Inter-Electrode Distance for a Plane-Plane Electrode Geometry Under Positive DC Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This experimental study focuses on the impact of temperature and inter-electrode distance on high-voltage breakdown voltage in the air, specifically for a planar-plane electrode configuration under positive DC voltage. Precise measurements of the breakdown voltage were conducted at different ambient temperatures and inter-electrode distances. The results reveal a significant increase in breakdown voltage with the inter-electrode distance, while it decreases with the rise in temperature. These observations align with established theories on breakdown in gases. The in-depth analysis of experimental data provides essential insights into the underlying physical mechanisms of the high-voltage breakdown phenomenon in the air. These findings substantially contribute to a better understanding of electrical discharges in high-voltage systems and can be applied in the design and optimization of electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Theoretical Comparative Study of the Band Offset and Band Offset Ratio of the GaNAsSb/GaAs and GaNAsSb/GaSb Quantum Well Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The aim of this work is to investigate the band alignment and offset ratio configurations of GaNAsSb on GaAs and GaSb substrates. The BAC (band anti-crossing) model and Model Solid theory are used to obtain the band gap energy and band offsets, respectively. The effect of adding N and Sb to the host material will be tested to maximize the potential of these material systems and provide the best material system suitable for long wavelength emission.

articleTitle: Development of a Means for Controlling the Uplink Signal Generator at the Algerian Satellite Ground Station
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This article presents the development of a software intended to drive the radiofrequency (RF) signal generator model TGR2050, specifically used for the S-band uplink communications of the ALSAT-1B satellite ground station. The software is capable of automatically generating a modulated signal covering the generator frequency range, from 150 kHz to 2000 MHz, to produce an uncompensated Doppler frequency of approximately 70 MHz. Its integration into the Oran S/X band station and its validation on the ALSAT-B satellite have demonstrated its effectiveness, guaranteeing successful transmission of commands (TC) and continuous telemetry (TM).

articleTitle: Three-Phase Switched Capacitor Boost Inverter for Photovoltaic Pumping Systems with Adapted Space Vector Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a Three-phase Switched Capacitor Boost Inverter controlled by an Adapted Space Vector Modulation technique to drive an induction motor for pumping systems. This structure eliminates the need for bulky DC/DC boost converters by integrating three cascaded switched capacitor units within the inverter. This clever integration not only boosts the input DC voltage and achieves higher gains but also reduces weight, and volume, and minimizes power losses. The adapted Space Vector Modulation with its dynamic modulation index based on the operating mode of the structure, enables the three-phase switched capacitor Boost Inverter to operate at extended voltage ranges for enhanced photovoltaic pumping efficiency. The switched capacitor Boost Inverter operating modes and control scheme are explained and the simulation results are presented, discussed, and validated experimentally under constant and dynamic operating conditions.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Swing-Up PD and Sliding Mode Control for Rotary Inverted Pendulum
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper investigates the stabilization of a Rotary Inverted Pendulum (RIP) using two control methods: a proportional-derivative (PD) controller and a novel sliding mode controller (SMC). This system presents significant control challenges. Its dynamical equations are highly non-linear, coupled, and complex. Additionally, it is underactuated. Therefore, the goal is to regulate the pendulum's arm of the RIP from a hanging position to its upright equilibrium point and maintain stability despite external disturbances. A swing-up PD controller, a common approach based on energy for RIP control, is first implemented. This controller successfully maneuvers the arm upright. Subsequently, a SMC type is designed to handle the system's non-linear dynamics directly, achieving stabilization without the need for a swing-up technique, unlike the PD controller. Experimental results using the QUBE-Servo platform from Quanser are presented and compared to demonstrate the performance of the two controllers in stabilizing the RIP.

articleTitle: Lidar Approach for Vehicular Applications in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This work purpose was to design a Light Detection and Ranging system called Lidar for vehicular networks applications. The proposed system is based on the use of 2D OCDMA codes to design a Lidar sensor. It's performance has been studied with reference to the Q factor, the Bit Error Rate (BER) and the eye diagram, as evaluation aspects.

articleTitle: Smart Food Sorting Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Food quality detection refers to the process of evaluating and assessing the characteristics, properties, and safety of food products to determine their overall quality. It ensures that the food is free from harmful contaminants, such as bacteria and viruses. Traditional methods involve various testing techniques to identify potential issues related to safety and nutritional value. However, these methods often require manual labor, resulting in extended detection times and laborious processes. Food fruit sorting techniques, on the other hand, are methods used to categorize and separate fruits based on attributes such as size, color, shape, ripeness, and quality. In this article, we present an embedded system remotely connected to a server-trained model for fruit image classification using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) deep learning algorithm. The accuracy of the model reached 94% in the validation set. The embedded system is based on a Raspberry Pi microcontroller equipped with a camera, enabling real-time sorting of fruits into six categories: fresh orange, fresh banana, fresh apple, rotten banana, rotten apple, and rotten orange. Additionally, it incorporates a weight sensor to determine the total weight of each category.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Different Local Descriptors for Maritime Ships Recognition using Bag of Visual Words Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Infrared maritime ship recognition is the process of identifying ships in infrared images for the purposes of maritime surveillance, navigation safety, and environmental protection. This task can be accomplished using a variety of methods, including handcrafted feature extraction. In this paper, we aim to create a global representation of manually extracted local features from infrared images by using the same methodology for extraction and classification. The purpose is to provide a comprehensive comparison of different descriptors such us; SURF, KAZE, ORB and BRISK. The results of this study indicate that the ORB descriptors performed better than the other descriptors (SURF, KAZE and BRISK) used in this methodology when combining vector equalization encoding, bag of visual words and spatial pyramid matching technique to have a global representation of object in infrared imagery. This was due to ORB being able to represent the highest number of features in an image compared to the other descriptors.

articleTitle: Factors Affecting the Adhesion Force in Electrostatic Separation of Metal/Plastic Mixtures Using an Electric Curtain Conveyor with Suction System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Electric curtain conveyors, which are widely used for the displacement of dielectric particles, have proven their feasibility in the electrostatic separation of a mixture (metal/plastic). The aim of this work is to achieve a new technique of separating a mixture of particles (metal/plastic) using a three-phase electric curtain conveyor ECC. This technique is based on the electrical attraction force and the air suction force using a three-phase ECC and an aspirator, so that the metal parts remain attached to the surface of the ECC under the effect of the attraction force, while the plastic particles are aspirated by the aspirator. An experimental study was carried out on stainless - steel metal parts studying the influence of several parameters on their attachment such as the electrode width and the gap spacing and air flow. Regarding the numerical part, a numerical modeling of the electric field was done to specify the seat of the attraction force. The numerical results obtained clearly explained the behavior of metal parts on the surface of different ECC configurations.

articleTitle: 3 to 6 GHz CMOS LC VCO Design for PLL of Cognitive Radio Application
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of a wideband LC Voltage-Controlled Oscillator (VCO) tailored for cognitive radio applications. The VCO, employing a complementary cross-coupled LC topology in Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) 65nm technology, spans over a wide frequency range from 3.46 GHz to 6.33 GHz, equipped with fine and coarse tuning capabilities. Behavioral model of a charge pump PLL is constructed using Verilog-A, enabling a high-level simulation of system performance and facilitating the evaluation of the designed VCO. The VCO displays good performance, with a minimum phase noise of -120 dBc/Hz @1MHz and a low power consumption of 4 mW.

articleTitle: Modeling. Simulation, and Optimization of Photoconductive Antennas According to the Gap Size
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In the present work, we review and analyze the most widely adopted theoretical models to characterize the radiated terahertz pulse in photoconductive antennas, with a focus on the impact of antenna gap size, small gap, and large gap. Furthermore, based on the reviewed models, we have conducted simulations to investigate the impact of various antenna parameters on the terahertz radiation performance, including semiconductor substrate characteristics, exciting femtosecond laser parameters, and the applied bias voltage. In addition, to provide a structured approach, we have proposed a flowchart outlining the steps for evaluating, and optimizing photoconductive antenna performance. Simulation results permit a well understanding of the contributing parameters' influence on the terahertz radiation. Finally, we have demonstrated the discrepancy arising from inappropriate modeling by comparing experimental measurements of a small gap antenna with simulations based on both small and large gap models. The results showcase a high degree of agreement between the small gap antenna simulations and experimental data, while the large gap model exhibits significant discrepancies. This underscores the importance of employing the appropriate model for accurate antenna performance analysis and optimization which is not satisfied in many recent published papers.

articleTitle: Enhancing Application Placement in Cloud-Fog Environment Based on Multicriteria Decision Making
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Fog computing (FC) is a distributed infrastructure computing that extends cloud computing (CC) capabilities to the edge of the network, closer to where data is generated and consumed. This approach responds to the challenges caused by Internet of Things (IoT) applications, which generate massive amounts of data that are costly and time-consuming to send to the cloud for processing. By leveraging fog computing, the cloud's limitations were successfully addressed, such as unpredictable latency. However, this shift introduced a new challenge. One of these challenges is finding the best placement of applications on distributed fog devices. This paper outlines a study aimed at addressing this challenge by utilizing multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) techniques, including the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). This study aims to choose the most appropriate fog nodes for positioning and processing application modules. The simulation was carried out on the iFogSim simulator, and the findings indicate that the suggested technique provides significant improvements in placement time and latency in a fog computing environment.

Author Keywords: Internet of Things (IoT) - Fog Computing - Cloud Computing - Resource Management - Application Placement-MCDM - TOPSIS - AHP - iFogSim

articleTitle: Grey Wolf Optimization to Boost the Efficiency of CdTe Based Thin Film Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a thorough theoretical exploration into the efficiency limitations of CdTe solar cells. Our investigation aims to understand how various parameters influence device performance. We introduce a model that integrates a GWO-based optimization approach, allowing for the optimal adjustment of both geometric and electrical parameters in thin-film solar cells. By strategically optimizing the properties of both CdTe and CdS materials, we demonstrate the potential to achieve an efficiency of up to 24.25%. Our optimized design surpasses the baseline, achieving a high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J_{SC}$</tex> of 21.44 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{mA}/\mathbf{cm}^{2},Voc$</tex> of 1.38 V, and FF of 82%. This approach represents a groundwork for further design enhancements.

articleTitle: Allocation Analysis Optimal of Energy Storage System in Grid Connected Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This example shows a low voltage network with different network areas with four battery energy storage systems with their respective control functionality, decentral energy resources (DER) and charging infrastructure. The focus of the example is the enhanced modeling of equipment (network elements) for the power flow and time series calculation using on the one hand the default controllers (e.g. to model the voltage-dependent reactive power control of inverters) and on the other hand the usage of individual models (designed in the graphical model builder). The necessary modeling steps, the input of the calculation parametsers as well as the different possibilities to display and evaluate the calculation results are shown in the example network.

articleTitle: Analysis and OGY Control of Chaotic Dynamics in Cancer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this study, we control the dynamic model representing the interaction among tumor, host and immune cells using the OGY method with 1D mapping. This technique, applied to control chaos in dynamical systems by strategically adjusting control parameters. Using MATLAB for simulations, we demonstrate the potential of the OGY method to knowing the appropriate timing and dosage of therapeutic interventions, with the goal of guiding the system towards a healthier state. Our results highlight the method's ability to stabilize chaotic dynamics of cancer model with minimal perturbations, leading to more precise and effective treatment strategies.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of a Low-Pressure Glow Discharge Characteristics in a Thin Film Deposition Plasma Reactor
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The work carried out in this paper falls within the framework of fundamental research on electrical discharges. Thus, the work of this paper is focused on the study of the electrical characteristics of electroluminescent discharges in a plasma reactor intended for the deposition of thin metallic film. The discharges are established under low pressure in a rare gas, which is Argon. The experimental study showed that the decrease in the inter-electrode distance or the gas pressure allows to change the discharge regime towards the regime of the abnormal electroluminescent discharge, which is more energetic and suitable for the deposition of the thin film. In addition, the analysis of the experimental breakdown voltage curves in the reactor revealed that Paschen's law is not verified and requires further studies on the effect of the shape and size of the electrodes as well as on the type of electrode materials used in the reactor.

articleTitle: Impact of Temperature on Skin Depth and Crossover Frequency in Conductive Materials Considering Reflection Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of temperature on skin depth and crossover frequency in conductive materials, employing laws such as Matthiessen’ s Law, the Curie-Weiss Law, and Curie's Law to integrate temperature effects into skin depth calculations. The research explores how temperature variations affect electrical conductivity, magnetic permeability, and dielectric permittivity. By incorporating these properties into the skin depth formula, the study provides a comprehensive analysis of how these factors influence electromagnetic wave penetration. The examination of metals such as aluminum, copper, platinum, and tin highlights the increase in skin depth with rising temperatures. This research offers a framework for understanding and predicting the effects of temperature on skin depth in conductive materials, thereby aiding the development of more effective electromagnetic applications and material management.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Reconfigurable Direct Digital Linear Chirp Synthesizer For Software Defined Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper introduces a new FPGA-based scheme to implement a reconfigurable LFM signal synthesizer for software-defined radar applications. This new approach is based on the DDCS algorithm. The proposed implementation architecture is designed to avoid additional comparison operations of the instantaneous frequency to the upper limit frequency in the modulation process compared to the existing DDCS architecture. Consequently, it results in lower logic utilization and higher flexibility. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is validated through simulation, implementation, and real-time hardware verification. This reveals our implementation approach's efficiency, flexibility, and adaptability compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Output Neural Network-Based Online Filter Parameters Estimation for Predictive Control of PWM Converter Under Unbalanced Grid Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Predictive current control (PCC) of a grid-connected pulsewidth modulation converter is highly effective under ideal grid voltage conditions with accurate parameters. However, under unbalanced grid conditions, conventional PCC can lead to significant power ripple and current harmonics. This deterioration is aggravated when the inductance and resistance values of the input filter deviate from their actual values, compromising system performance. This paper introduces a novel multioutput ADALINE (MO-ADALINE) structure, which combines a multi-output adaptive neural identifier (MO-ANI) to estimate the input parameters accurately and an adaptive neural filter to process the input signals of the MO-ANI. This configuration facilitates real-time identification and insures precise estimation of input filter parameters under unbalanced grid conditions. To further enhance PCC performance, the symmetrical decomposition of the grid voltages is employed, aiming to ensure sinusoidal grid currents and minimize active power ripples. Simulation results validate the efficiency of the proposed approach, which provides robust and good dynamics in terms of response time and ripple reduction.

articleTitle: SMO Based Sensorless Direct Torque Sliding Mode Control of IM for EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a study and analysis of a direct torque control strategy associated with a sliding mode control (DTC-SMC) without a speed sensor to control the four induction motors used for the propulsion of a four-wheel drive electric vehicle 4WDEV. The estimation of the rotor speed of each motor is obtained by a sliding mode observer SMO. The main objective of this control method is to increase the robustness and reduce torque and stator flux oscillations. The model is made using the Matlab / Simulink environment. The simulation results obtained show the effectiveness of the control strategy in terms of driving cycle trajectory tracking and disturbance rejection.

articleTitle: 1Orange Freshness Classification Using Fluorescence and Color Imaging With Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Automatic fruit freshness categorization presents a challenging task in agriculture. In fact, this process is crucial for ensuring quality and meeting consumer expectation. In this work, particular attention is given to the spoilage of oranges, this phenomenon is caused by poor conservation methods leading to diseases, especially fungal infections. The aim of this study is to explore the use of the pretrained ResNet34 classification model, in combination with specifics imaging techniques to identify early signs of spoilage in oranges. Two imaging techniques are employed: traditional color imaging under white light and fluorescence imaging under UV light at 365 nm. The obtained results highlight the superior efficacy of fluorescence imaging in detecting spoilage, achieving an accuracy rate of 76.92%, compared to 65.38% with color imaging.

articleTitle: Robust Control Strategy for an Electric Water Pump Powered by the Photovoltaic Panel
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this paper we present a robust control strategy for an electric centrifugal pump (ECP) for water powered by a photovoltaic system. To drive this pump, we use a Brushless direct current motor (BLDCM). We also adopted a robust vector control of BLDCM based on fractional order proportional-integral controller (FOPI). The idea is to maintain the motor speed constant within a well-determined interval of fluctuation in the voltage supplied by the photovoltaic panel (PV). simulation results clearly show the feasibility of the proposed control system of DC Brushless motor.

Author Keywords: Brush less permanent-magnet direct current motor (BLDCM)

articleTitle: Underground Electric Field Radiated by Lightning Return Stroke on Tall Sructures: Analysis Using EM Models and the 3D-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this study, we present an analysis of the underground propagation relative to the vertical and horizontal electrical fields, generated by the interaction between lightning and a tall object, namely a tower erected on a finite conductivity ground. The effect of the soil depth on the propagation of electrical field is taken into account in this study. The tower under consideration has resemblance to the Peissenberg Tower built in Germany. Simulation results are obtained by using electromagnetic models of the lightning current. These models are associated to the three-dimensional finite differences in time domain (3D-FDTD) method based on Taflove formulation and the the UPML limit conditions. A computing code is developed in Matlab based on the suggested approach. Three distinct distances from the bottom of the tower were taken into account and in the calculation, we considered two different depths. Finally, the findings highlighted that the suggested approach is an effective method for assessing and analyzing lightning underground electrical fields.

articleTitle: Improvement of the Conversion Quality and Efficiency of a Two-Stage Single-Phase Photovoltaic Microinverter
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This article aims to present improvements made to a two-stage single-phase photovoltaic micro-inverter, the Symmetrical Boost-Discharge. The first stage is based on a Boost converter and a discharge circuit that provides a rectified sine voltage. The second stage is a bridge inverter that reverses the second half-cycle. This inverter exhibits good performance in terms of current and voltage harmonic distortion rates, with the existing harmonic distortion largely caused by voltage error during zero crossing. The enhancements to the micro-inverter aim to ensure a better zero crossing using a compensation circuit placed in series with the first stage of the inverter. This circuit generates a voltage equal to the inverter voltage error, ensuring that the series connection eliminates the output voltage error and thus ensures a better zero crossing. This paper includes the model, sizing, and stability study of the added circuit, as well as presenting results under resistive and inductive load conditions.

articleTitle: Performances Analysis of DNN Accelerator in a HW/SW Co-Design FPGA Implementation for Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a proof of concept illustrating the deployment of a trained Deep Neural Network (DNN) on Zedboard FPGA for the purpose of image classification across Edge Computing (EC) devices. The training has been achieved in python environment, while the architecture has been validated using a HW/SW codesign approach achieving an accuracy of 97.36% applied on MNIST dataset for digits recognition. The core of the design has been designed by making use of open-source ZyNet python package. The testing has been conducted successfully and the design has shown its capacity to recognize more than one digit image at the entry of the DNN. An extensive performances evaluation has been conducted in terms of accuracy, influence of key parameters and resources utilization. The design has achieved a throughput of 4.608 Gbps.

articleTitle: Making Biometric Identification with EMG Easier: Using a Single Channel for Specific Purposes
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: EMG has become a powerful method that was first used to identify muscle disorders in medical settings. Now, EMG signals are being used in a new way to identify people. Most biometric methods use complex systems with many channels, which makes them hard to use in real life. This study challenges this idea by suggesting that identification can be done with just one EMG channel for a smaller group of people. We explain how to collect, preprocess, and enhance data for EMG-based identification. We use a stacked Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network to classify EMG signals accurately and effectively. Our results show high accuracy and F1 scores equal to 96.4, which means our approach works well. This research not only improves EMG-based identification systems but also has potential uses in biometrics and other areas.

articleTitle: Consensus Analysis with Time Delays in Variable Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper delves into consensus issues within undirected networked systems. The convergence of nodes under various network assumptions is examined, considering differing agent numbers, diverse topologies, and constant time-delays. Additionally, there are two main pieces of information gained from simulations. The first is algebraic connectivity, which determines the speed at which consensus can be achieved. The second reveals the network's tolerance to time delays. These findings highlight a crucial relationship between network structure and information flow. They offer valuable insights into how consensus dynamics and resilience operate within networked systems, along with practical suggestions for implementation.

articleTitle: Correlation Between Frequency and Water Trees Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study aims to enhance the detection of water tree defects in polymeric insulation by analyzing the potential and field distribution on an electrical cable outer layer. The examination focuses on vented water trees originating from the outer semiconducting layer of the cable model under investigation. Specifically, we are keen on exploring the influence of frequency and lift-off (the distance between the sensor and the target) on the sensitivity to detect water trees within the internal insulation of the electrical cable. In order to accomplish this, we selected two frequency ranges: the low frequencies, comprising the values of 1 Hz, 10 Hz, 20 Hz, 30 and 50 Hz, and the high frequencies, covering 1 kHz, 10 kHz, 50 kHz, and 100 kHz. Additionally, we considered various lift-off distances of 0 mm, 0.5 mm, 1 mm, and 1.5 mm. The numerical model is implemented under COMSOL MULTIPHYSICS environment, using the finite element method.

articleTitle: Realization and Optimization of a Rotating Cylinder Separator
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: There are several devices designed for the processing of millimeter-sized granular mixtures, but few devices are specifically designed for the treatment of micronized particles. That's why a rotating cylinder separator has been developed to address this specific need. This separator stands out by not requiring a tribocharging device. Instead, it utilizes the charge acquired by the particles during the grinding process to separate them. To ensure its proper functioning, the separator requires an electrode cleaning system, such as a brush connected to the electrode. The objective of this study was to assess the impact of various elements that may affect the new electrostatic separator's performance. Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and unplasticized polyvinyl chloride (UPVC) were combined in a binary mixture for the experiments. Three control factors were examined: the applied high voltage, the particle flow rate, and the cylinder's rotation speed. The purity measurement was carried out using a visual method. The obtained results were extremely satisfactory, confirming the effectiveness of this equipment

articleTitle: Development of Sn-ZnO Thin Films for Energy Storage Uses
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study concentrates on the development of thin films composed of undoped and tin doped zinc oxide (Sn-ZnO) deposited on glass substrates using the spray pyrolysis method. Different methods of characterization, including X-ray diffraction (XRD), were employed to analyze the structural, optical, and electrical properties of the resulting films. XRD analysis confirmed that all samples possess polycrystalline films with a hexagonal wurtzite structure characterized by the P 63 mc space group. This indicates a well-defined crystalline structure for both undoped and doped Sn-ZnO. Impedance spectroscopy was utilized to investigate the impact of varying Sn concentrations on the electrical behavior of the films across a frequency range of 10 Hz to 100 kHz. Notably, all sample exhibited low loss tangent values, indicating their suitability for energy storage and photovoltaic applications.

articleTitle: The Impact of the Opto-Geometic Parameter of A Salinity Sensor Based on Photonic Crsytal Fiber on Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This article examined a salinity sensor based on photonic crystal fiber. We report results of two numerical study on two salinity sensors for seawater, using a four rings microstructured fiber. We filled the first ring holes with seawater. We firstly calculate the salinity sensitivity by varying salt concentration from 0% to 100% for the first proposed sensor then for the second suggested sensor after changing the diameter of the first ring holes. Meanwhile, numerical simulations are used to examine the effects of different geometrical parameters on the sensing properties. Finally, it is noted that the sensitivity of the salt level in water as 0.021727 ps/(nm.km)/PSU.

articleTitle: Realization of a High-Voltage High-Frequency Power Supply for Ozone Generation. Application to Water Traitement
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: A high-voltage high-frequency power supply for ozone generation by dielectric barrier discharge is shown in this paper.
