Ozone generation is to be used in the air disinfection for small installations as well as in the water disinfection. The power supply comprises a power stage composed of a single-phase half-bridge inverter to regulate the power output, a driver circuit for MOSFET transistors based on a “push-pull” amplifier followed by a pulse transformer and a control block based on the timer 555. The converter topology is one of the most conventional and is intended to supply a high voltage transformer which feeds the ozone generator in particular, whose frequency depends on the three components devices (two resistors and a capacitor) of the timer 555. The results of the electrical characterization of the dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) supplied by the power supply and those obtained with a research spectrophotometer according to several processing time showed the reliability of the power supply.

articleTitle: Linear BLDC Motor Embeded Control on ESP32
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a linear Brushless DC (BLDC) motor, along with its drive and control system. The motor is powered by an embedded LiPo 4s battery and operates on a closed-loop rail equipped with permanent magnets (PM). The control program, developed in C, is executed on an ESP32 microcontroller. It also enables communication with smartphones and PCs via web sockets. This experimental setup serves as a versatile tool for educational purposes and research, facilitating the study of various aspects ranging from motor design to control strategies.

articleTitle: Detection of False Data Injection Attacks in Smart Power Grid Using Data Balancing-Based Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The state estimation technique in intelligent power systems is critical for estimating state variables based on appropriate measurement data. Nevertheless, this technique is exposed to cyber-attacks, the best known of which is the false data injection attack (FDIA), which poses a danger to advanced energy systems. This work describes a method for detecting fraudulent attacks using machine learning techniques that include Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), and Decision Tree (DT). Different oversampling approaches have been used to tackle the imbalanced dataset issue including the Random Oversampling Technique (ROT), Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) and Borderline SMOTE. The approach was applied to well-known Oak Ridge National Laboratory datasets. Various measures were used to analyze the efficiency of this study, including accuracy, F1-score, precision and recall.

Author Keywords: imbalanced dataset. Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL)

articleTitle: A 3D Integral Model Using Fictitious Surface Currents for the Magnetic Field Modeling in Ferromagnetic Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a 3-D integral modeling approach of ferromagnetic parts when solving static equations using integral methods. This approach involves considering a position-dependent equivalent surface current distribution. The proposed approach is applied to calculate the magnetic flux density distribution in a ferromagnetic block with finite relative permeability. The results obtained are compared with the finite element method, showing that the approach accurately takes into account the relative permeability.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Air Conditioning System in Solar Home for Peak Demand Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper introduces and discusses a Demand-Side Management (DSM) strategy for optimizing energy use produced by the photovoltaic power plant of a solar house to meet its energy needs. This study focuses on scheduling the air conditioner's operating time to synchronize its start-up with peak production from the photovoltaic (PV) power plant. The present work aims to smooth out recurring peaks in energy demand during the summer season. It is shown that the proposed strategy enables a saving of around 45% on energy amount, usually drawn from the grid to operate the air conditioner in order to maintain a set indoor temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$24^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. A reduction of around 35% in Peak Power Demand (PMD) on the national interconnected grid during the summer period could be achieved if Algerian households are equipped with PV power plants for electricity generation, and if a DSM strategy is applied to air-conditioning operation.

articleTitle: Development of a High-Frequency Power Source Dedicated to DBD Reactors for Ozone Production
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a half-bridge resonant inverter to power a dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) ozone generator. We use the PIC16F876A microcontroller-based control circuit to vary the inverter frequency. We use a step-up transformer to obtain the high voltage required for the DBD. We conducted an experimental study to investigate the impact of frequency and voltage on ozone production and power consumption. The results show that these two parameters have a strong influence. This study demonstrates the advantages of using a resonant inverter combined with optimum electrical parameter adjustment to achieve excellent energy efficiency for the DBD ozone generator. The choice of a resonant half-bridge topology aims to maximize energy efficiency, crucial in a solar-powered system. The circuit has been optimized to reduce switching losses. In addition, the development of the power source takes into account the capacitive nature of DBD reactors, using a series resonant circuit formed by the DBD capacitance and the step-up transformer inductance. The frequency range from 14 kHz to 17.5 kHz has been specifically chosen and optimized for the DBD reactor, taking into account the constraints of the PV source and the characteristics of the discharge.

articleTitle: Comparative Study Between an Analytical Model and Simulation of a Magnetic Induction in an Eddy Current Separator
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The process of eddy current separation (ECS) is widely employed in the scrap recycling industry to separate nonferrous metals from nonmetallic materials. Nevertheless, the conceptual framework of eddy current separation (ECS) has traditionally leaned towards empirical approximations, numerical simulations, and an analytical model. This paper aims to conduct a straightforward comparative study between an analytical model and a simulation of an eddy current separator, utilizing finite element method software and MATLAB.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Potential of $BaLa_{2}ZnO_{5}\ : \ Er^{3+}$ LEDs for Overcoming NLOS Challenges in VLC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Visible Light Communication (VLC) is a promising wireless data transfer paradigm that uses light waves to provide high-speed communication in indoor environments. In Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) scenarios, where the direct line-of-sight (LOS) between transmitter and receiver is obstructed, VLC offers unique advantages over traditional radio frequency (RF) communication, including increased security and reduced interference. In this paper, we investigate the influence of quantum efficiency (QE) of LEDs on the performance of VLC systems, particularly in NLOS situations. Using OptiSystem software Version 19, we conduct thorough modeling and analysis of the VLC NLOS model for both conventional LEDs and Barium Lanthanum Zinc Oxide doped with Erbium <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Er^{3+})$</tex> ions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(BaLa_{2}ZnO_{5}\ : \ Er^{3+})$</tex> LEDs. Our comparative study highlights the superior performance of the proposed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BaLa_{2}ZnO_{5}\ : \ Er^{3+}$</tex> LED, achieving a Q-Factor of 6.63 and a lower Bit Error Rate (BER) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.17\times 10^{-12}$</tex>. These results elucidate the impact of QE on key performance metrics such as BER, Q-Factor, and signal distortion, emphasizing the crucial role of QE in improving the reliability and efficiency of VLC systems. Opening the path for future advances in wireless communication technology.

articleTitle: Magneto-Hydrodynamic Coupling of a Sea Wave Energy Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In recent decades, the world has faced escalating challenges of energy shortages and environmental pollution. Cutting-edge technologies for harnessing renewable energy, such as wave energy, are viewed as pivotal solutions to these issues. Among these, the Wave Energy Converter (WEC) emerges as one of the most efficient and promising methods for capturing and utilizing wave energy. This article discusses the modeling and analysis of the wave energy harvesting system. This system is composed of a Tubular Linear Permanent Magnets Generator with (TLPMG) operating thanks to the kinetic energy obtained by the vibration of the sea waves. The model developed is based on the governing equations of the magnetic field expressed in terms of magnetic vector potential and magnetic scalar potential solved by the finite element method. The coupling is carried out sequentially between the electromagnetic and mechanical equations obtained after hydrodynamic modeling of the system. Wave vibration cycles are transmitted to the device in the form of vertical displacements. The results obtained are mainly the displacement, the speed the floating buoy, Excitation force and electromotive force.

articleTitle: Waste Sorting Automation with Visual Sensor and RFID
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The quantity of domestic wastes is constantly increasing, resulting on overload of wastes. Recycling became imperative for ecologic and economical considerations in order to apply circular economy rules. In general, humans are recruited in waste sorting plants for performing the dangerous and tedious sorting tasks. The automation is, thus, necessary. This paper deals with the problem of waste sorting automation. The proposed solution consists of waste recognition and classification using YOLOv8, and human presence detection using RFID (Radio frequency Identification) tags. The proposed solution is validated in simulation. The virtual robot performs a task in order to simulate the behavior of a real robot with high fidelity, depending on the information coming from the RFID tags and a visual sensor.

articleTitle: Prediction of Brain Tumor Volume Based on Segmented Slices
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Detection and accurate segmentation of brain tumors play an important role in medical diagnosis and treatment planning. In this study, we present a comprehensive analysis of different parts of brain tumors, focusing on the prediction of tumor volume. This research introduces a novel algorithm that enables the estimation of tumor volume based on medical images (MRI) segmented using U-Net with improved accuracy. By using advanced computational techniques in image processing, we aim to improve the understanding and characterization of brain tumor components. Recent advances in this methodology have allowed us to accurately measure the size of tumors. By obtaining accurate measurements of tumor size, medical professionals can make more informed decisions about treatment options and monitor the effectiveness of interventions over time. This study represents a significant advancement in the interpretation of MRI images for the detection and volumetric assessment of brain tumors.

articleTitle: 39 GHz Double Negative DR-SRR 5G mm-Wave Applications Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This research presents a metamaterial design using a double rectangular split ring resonator (DR-SRR) configuration to enhance electromagnetic characteristics for 5G millimeter-wave (mmWave) applications. Drawing on design principles from WiMAX and WLAN literature, this study adapts these insights to the 5G spectrum, particularly at 39 GHz. The chosen design prioritizes a simple structure for ease of realization and cost-effectiveness. Computer Simulation Technology (CST-2021) is used to thoroughly evaluate the efficiency of this metamaterial structure. The compact design, measuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$((0.32\times 0.36\times 0.026)),2.51 \times 2.82 \times 0.289(\text{mm}^{3})$</tex>, is implemented on a Rogers RT /Duroid 5880 substrate and undergoes a comprehensive parametric study to optimize its parameters. CST facilitates generation of scattering parameters, enabling examination of negative effective permittivity and permeability, along with the distribution of current surface, electric, and magnetic fields. Additionally, performance assessment involves tests using various array configurations, such as 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 2,2\times 2,3\times 1,3\times 2$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 3$</tex> arrays. All configurations show satisfactory agreement with the proposed metamaterial's potential suitability for 5G mm Wave applications. The proposed design reaches a bandwidth of over 3 GHz, showing a significant presence of electric and magnetic field components. It also demonstrates negative permittivity, permeability, and refractive index characteristics, establishing it as a Double Negative (DNG) metamaterial.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of Surface Charge Dynamics of Corona Charged Polymers
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this study, we investigated the surface electric charge decay of polyimide film subjected to corona discharge conditions using the unipolar charge transport model. This model incorporates different processes such as charge injection, migration, trapping and detrapping. Several parameters were examined, including carrier mobility and trapping and detrapping coefficients, which are crucial in determining charge transport behavior in polyimide film. The unipolar charge transport model was analyzes by solving a system of equations involving continuity equations coupled with the Poisson equation and the transport equation. These equations elucidate the transport phenomena occurring within the polyimide film and their correlation with surface potential decay. The main finding of the study is the consistent decrease in surface potential over time, indicating a gradual dissipation of charge within the polyimide film. This decay in surface potential is influenced by various parameters such as carrier mobility and trapping and detrapping coefficients.

articleTitle: Predictive Method for Cleaning Photovoltaic Plants in Desert Areas Using TinyML and IoT Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this work, a predictive method for planning the cleaning of photovoltaic (PV) plants is proposed, especially for desert areas where dust and sand are frequently observed. A dataset of visual images of PV modules was collected and used. It consisted of three classes (clean, dust accumulation, and sand deposit on PV modules). The Edge impulse platform has been used to develop the classifier, and based on the predicted class, we can determine the cleaning period (daily, weekly, or monthly) and type of cleaning process. Subsequently, the model was quantized and implemented into a low-cost microcontroller (Nano BLE Sense). To assist the user in making a decision regarding the cleaning plan, the obtained classification results were posted on a platform (Arduino IoT cloud) using a low-cost WiFi module (ESP8266). Co-simulation and experimental tests demonstrated the feasibility of the proposed method, and the outdoor test was held in the Sahara region of Algeria.

articleTitle: Video Transcoding Dataset for MPEG-DASH MPD Generation: An Experimental Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The preparation of video content for MPEG-DASH MPD (Media Presentation Description) generation is the first step in the MPEG-DASH process. It is crucial for ensuring seamless adaptive streaming experiences for users. There are many datasets in the literature that include various video attributes, encoding parameters, and quality metrics that can be utilized to evaluate video preparation strategies. In this article, we describe how to create a dataset for this particular task using objective parameters: PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) and SSIM (Structural Similarity Index).

articleTitle: Stimulated Raman Scattering in Silica Tapered Nanofibers Within Nonlinear Liquid Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Optical nanofibers have emerged as versatile devices for exploring nonlinear optical processes, thanks to their robust evanescent fields and light-confining capabilities. This study investigates evanescent stimulated Raman scattering in a silica optical nanofiber submerged in various mixtures of nonlinear liquids at a wavelength of 1064 nm. To illustrate the impact of nonlinear liquid composition on scattering properties, we analyze factors such as the liquid's refractive index, Raman gain coefficient, and volume ratio for a Raman-active liquid, which is Benzene mixed with Cyclohexane or Perfluorohexane. Employing numerical modeling to examine the interaction between guided modes transmitted through the optical nanofiber and the surrounding nonlinear liquid, we estimate optimal Raman liquid volume fractions and nanofiber radii to maximize modal Raman gain. The potential applications of stimulated Raman scattering in optical nanofibers include telecommunications, wavelength conversion, optical sensing, and signal amplification.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Shielding Effectiveness in Conducting Polymer Composites Using the Transmission Line Matrix Method: Applications in Near and Far Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Conducting polymer composites offer a promising substitute for conventional shielding materials. The aim of this work is to provide a theoretical study contribution of the single and multilayer composite materials for electromagnetic shielding effectiveness (SE) in the near field and far field applications. The transmission line matrix formalism method is employed to simulate the (SE) of composite structures across both lower and higher frequency ranges. This method relies on calculating the crossover frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{c})$</tex> for each layer in the multilayered structure. The proposed single-layer configuration consists of a conductive polymer shield made from Polyaniline/Polyurethane (PANI/PU), while the multilayer shields are constructed using an Aluminum-(Polyaniline/Polyurethane)-Aluminum (AL-PANI/PU-AL) configuration. An analysis of the reflection loss, absorption loss, multiple reflection, and the (SE) is performed for both electrically thin and electrically thick scenarios.

articleTitle: Evaluation the Electrical Properties of XLPE Cable Insulation Material Aged Under the Combined Effects of Thermal Stress and UV-Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) is widely used as insulation material for power cables. In spite of its outstanding mechanical and electrical characteristics, XLPE may undergo degradation under service conditions. It is well known that temperature and UV radiations are the most aggressive stresses inducing degradation in XLPE insulation, especially under oxidative conditions (air). In this paper, the combined effects of thermal and accelerated UV-radiation aging on the dielectric properties of XLPE specimen used as power cables insulation material have been investigated. The resulting structural deteriorations were quantified by measuring and evaluating the dielectric permittivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon^{\prime})$</tex>, dielectric loss factor (tanδ) and dielectric loss index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon^{\prime\prime})$</tex> as function of aging time and frequency. Experimental results showed that the XLPE structure and related physical properties are considerably affected by the combined aging. Indeed, it was found that the dielectric parameters of XLPE are significantly changed as functions of aging time and frequency.

articleTitle: Localization of Buried Objects Under Pillar Using Ultra-Wideband Confocal Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this study, we provide an analysis of the accurate localization and geometric parameters of a buried bar within a concrete pillar across different frequency ranges. Several simulations have been performed using a monostatic configuration for ultrawideband based confocal imaging radar. The dimensions and dielectric properties of the background concrete medium are considered. The resulting S-parameters obtained with and without buried targets across various frequency ranges are compared. These comparisons are used to suggest the buried target's existence, localization and geometric parameters. Finally, the performance in the presence of noise is evaluated.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Two-Wire Corona Electrodes on Polypropylene Granule Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This research explores advancements in the electrostatic charging process for granular substances through an innovative two-wire corona electrode configuration. The study focuses on polypropylene granules and analyzes the impact of wire spacing and applied voltage on current-voltage characteristics and surface potential distributions. The results indicate that increased wire spacing amplifies corona discharge, and a higher number of wires at a fixed voltage increase the current on the ground electrode. Additionally, faster granule movement correlates with decreased surface potential, shedding light on the interplay between speed, exposure time, and charge efficiency. The research contributes to the understanding of electrostatic separation, providing insights that could improve industrial sorting processes.

articleTitle: HT-IDS:A Hybrid Trust Based Intrusion Detection System for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSN) are a continuously developing area of research with numerous applications. Despite their benefits, these networks present several challenges, including security problems. The trust factor is an effective strategy for securing the network against internal attacks and misbehaviour nodes. While several intrusion detection systems (IDSs) have been proposed, most of them consider either trust technique or anomaly detection technique. In this research, we suggested a hybrid intrusion detection system that takes anomaly detection techniques and trust factors into account. First, we proposed several criteria to model nodes' behaviours using multiple trust features. Then, we used the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm to classify their behaviour in the network. Our simulation results demonstrate that our approach can effectively detect malicious nodes in the network.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study Between (PVT) Collectors Based on Thin Film Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: PVT collectors are a significant technology that merges photovoltaic and solar collectors in order to produce both heat and electricity at the same time. The scientists investigated two distinct models of PVT collectors utilizing various configurations, with a focus on monocrystalline silicon. Additionally, there was a plan to explore a PVT collector depends binary, ternary, and quaternary materials found in thin-film solar cells to modify efficiency and lower costs. The study involves modeling a hybrid thermal photovoltaic (PVT) collector using thin-film solar cells by the Comsol 5.4 software. The results show an increase in temperature up to 95°C, fluid flow velocity reaching 0.00275 m/s, and an analysis of the electric current and power output of the PVT collector.

articleTitle: MMSE Channel Estimation in MIMO-FBMC/OQAM Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper focuses on preamble-based channel estimation in multiple-input multiple-output filterbank multicarrier based on offset quadrature amplitude modulation (MIMO-FBMC/OQAM). The most significant limitation of FBMC/OQAM systems is that orthogonality is only preserved in the real domain, leading to the appearance of intrinsic imaginary interference. In this paper, we construct a preamble that exploits the known intrinsic interference of the elements of the preamble and eliminates the unknown intrinsic interference generated by data to obtain better least square (LS) channel estimates at the pseudo pilot positions. The MIMO channels are estimated by minimum mean squared error (MMSE). The suggested estimator's effectiveness is validated by theoretical analysis and simulation results.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of STAR-RIS-Aided-V2V Visible Light Communications at Road Intersections
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In non-line-of-sight (NLOS) scenarios, especially at road intersections, vehicular visible light communication (V-VLC) systems often experience degraded performance. Obstacles like buildings, walls, nearby vehicles, and other obstructions hinder the exchange of safety messages between vehicles, impacting connectivity on perpendicular or parallel lanes. To tackle these challenges, we propose the implementation of a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) at road intersections. This approach aims to improve communication link reliability and provide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$360^{\circ}$</tex> coverage. Using a realistic channel model, we conduct a comprehensive performance analysis of the VLC links between the STAR-RIS and receiving vehicles. Performance metrics, including received power, bit error rate, and capacity, are evaluated for all the considered links. Our analysis results demonstrate that strategic deployment of the STAR-RIS at road intersections enables enhanced communication reliability and overcomes the limitations imposed by NLOS scenarios.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-Tube Ozone Generator Based on Dielectric Barrier Discharge for Wastewater Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This research introduces a new ozone generator called the multi-tube ozone generator. A comparative study of the electric field intensity is conducted between the simple ozone generator and the multi-tube ozone generator using the Comsol Multiphysics 5.6 simulation software. Analysis of the simulation results of the electric field intensity in both generators indicates that the multi-tube ozone generator exhibits a superior distribution of the electric field compared to the simple ozone generator. Based on these results, the new generator is used in treating wastewater. Experimental results regarding ozone concentration produced and wastewater treatment demonstrate the effectiveness of the new ozone generator.

articleTitle: Comparative Study for a Shunt Active Power Filter Using Multilevels Inverter with DSOGI-PLL
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study between Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) based on a Neutral Clamped Diode (NPC) three levels and NPC five levels inverter using Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) Dual Second Order Generalized Integrator phase locked loop (DSOGI - PLL) under unbalanced and distorted power grid system. SRF is the identification method for harmonics current with DSOGI-PLL method used to track and synchronize with the phase and frequency of the harmonics currents and recreate them as reference using the NPC three levels inverter and the NPC five levels inverter. This study allows also confirming the effectiveness of the DSOGI - PLL under non ideal conditions for the grid. The DC supply of the multilevel inverters is controlled and regulated by a PI controller. The following simulation using the interface MATLAB/SIMULINK and SimPowerSystem toolbox, confirms the success of the method by calculating the THD and comparing it to the IEEE standard.

articleTitle: PID Control Based on PSO for a Grid Connected Photovoltaic System Using a Three-Phase Voltage Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This article presents active and reactive control for a photovoltaic (PV) system connected to the grid based on designing and tuning a proportional-integral-derivative PID controller using a practical swarm optimization technique PSO. The (PV) system is connected to the grid utility by a three-phase voltage source inverter through an LCL filter to enhance the energy quality. Two controllers are used, a conventional proportional integral PI and a PID based on the PSO optimization technique (PID-PSO). The two controllers depend on the computation of instantaneous active and reactive powers from the voltage and current grid. The purpose of these controllers is to generate a control law that enables the PV system to operate at the desired performances. These controllers also guarantee the dynamic stability of the PV system in the presence of sudden irradiance changes on the PV generator and efficiently track the active power. The simulation results generated with MATLAB-Simulink reveal that the PID-PSO technique has superior dynamic performance regarding convergence time and overshoot compared to the standard PI controller.

Author Keywords: PID controller based on PSO technique

articleTitle: Study and Implementation of DTC-SVM Control of Five-Phase Induction Motor Fed by Five-Phase Voltage Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper introduces a well-known Direct Torque Control-Space Vector Modulation (DTC-SVM) approach for controlling a five-phase induction motor powered by a two-level, five-phase voltage source inverter. The proposed method employs two Proportional-Integral (PI) controllers to manage flux and torque. To assess the static and dynamic capabilities of the DTC-SVM technique, simulations were conducted using MATLAB/Simulink. Experimental trials were carried out on a custom-built test bench in the LCP laboratory of Ecole Nationale Polytechnique to corroborate the simulation outcomes and evaluate the actual efficacy of the control system. The DTC-SVM strategy demonstrated robust electrical and electromagnetic performance, adopting a constant switching frequency to mitigate a common issue associated with traditional DTC systems.

articleTitle: Green Synthesis of ZnO Nanostructures from Poppy-Leaf Extract Obteined by Spray Pyrolysis: Electrochemical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This work focuses on the green synthesis of nanostructures using plant extracts, combined with a pyrolysis spray method. The objective of this work is to study and characterize ZnO samples synthesized via green synthesis, specifically using Poppy-leaf extract, deposited on copper substrates by the pyrolysis spray growth process. The synthesized ZnO nanostructure has been characterized using different techniques such as, atomic force microscopy and electrochemistry. The J-V results indicate a higher current density for the ZnO nanostructure under light illumination. Furthermore, the EIS results suggest enhanced catalytic performance of the ZnO.

articleTitle: Medical Image Segmentation Based U-Net Architecture Implemented on Raspberry Pi4
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: U-net is an architecture that plays major role in medical image segmentation, which provides increased performance in the field of medical imaging. In this paper, we implement on Raspberry Pi4 deep convolutional neural networks for medicals images segmentation using U-Net architecture for region determination. Where the algorithm is implemented on Raspberry pi, and LCD Touchscreen is used to visualize and identify specific image regions. Graphical interface is developed to make the work easier for user. In our test two medical image datasets are chosen for segmentation task: Breast cancer Ultrasound Images Dataset (BUSI Dataset) and brain tumor MRI dataset. A U-Net model for breast cancer and tumor brain segmentation was trained and performances are evaluated by using Accuracy, Intersection over Union (IoU), Dice and Loss function.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of a Parallel Active Filter Considering Components Losses
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The increasing use of non-linear loads has raised concerns about disturbances in electrical networks. This paper examines the rise of parallel active filters (PAFs) in improving electrical power quality in response to the increase of this loads. To better approximate the real system, a loss estimation loop for semiconductor components was introduced. Harmonic current identification based on the instantaneous power method allows for the calculation of reference currents for the modulated hysteresis control of the PAF. Taking losses into account, the PAF is modeled and investigated with a nonlinear load using MATLAB/Simulink. The simulation results demonstrate the filter's effectiveness in attenuating harmonics and the influence of losses on the fundamental value of the current it delivers.

articleTitle: A New Electrostatic Separator Device Using a Double Side Rotating Actuator
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this work, a rotating actuator was employed to build a new electrostatic separator. This actuator is made of a double-layer Printed Circuit Board with a helical electrode on top side and a circular electrode on the bottom side. The separation efficiency of this device was evaluated using millimeter-sized copper/plastic particles. To get the optimum separation results, many parameters were investigated, including the level and shape of the voltage delivered to the electrodes. The collected data revealed that the best recovery and purity rates were reached.

articleTitle: Solar Distiller Production in Arid Climatic Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical and experimental study of a double-slope solar still with immersed fins (DSSS-FIB) to determine the impact of introducing of immersed fins in the basin. The conducted work examines the effects of the spacing between fins, fins height, fins number, and water layer thickness in the basin on the stagnant production. Increasing the fin height from 2 to 5 cm enhances the DSSS-FIB productivity, but a height increase from 6 to 8 cm results in a decrease in the DSSS-FIB distillate production. The distance between the fins shows no significant effect on the DSSS-FIB productivity. The results show that the suggested system's efficiency was about 15 to 27% greater than that of a basic system under the conditions: mw = 42.61 kg, h1 = 3.6 cm, Vv = 3.5 m/s, lw = 5 cm, and Nfins = 12.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracking Based on a Robust Backstepping Control for a Standalone Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) cells display behaviors in both voltage and power aspects necessitating the use of a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control method to enhance power extraction efficiency in varying environmental conditions. Therefore, this work introduces a robust non-linear backstepping approach for MPPT control in a photovoltaic system. The system design includes a panel array connected via a boost converter to a load. The control strategy dynamically adjusts and commands the converter's duty cycle to ensure that the output voltage and power in the photovoltaic array closely tracks a reference voltage thus optimizing power extraction. By conducting simulations, using MATLAB/Simulink our method performance was evaluated under different conditions. The outcomes show robustness, convergence response, minimal rise time low tracking errors and swift adaptation to environmental variations. To highlight the effectiveness and reliability of our control strategy we compared it with a PID control approach.

articleTitle: Facial Recognition Based on Machine and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Facial recognition technology plays a crucial role in enhancing security measures, providing accurate identification and authentication of individuals, thereby reducing the risk of unauthorized access and fraudulent activities. In this paper we propose an implementation of face recognition system using three datasets under uniform and complex background: Olivetti Research Laboratory (ORL), Computer Vison (CV) and Georgia Tech face database (Gt_Db). The system utilizes various machine and deep learning methods, including the Local Directional Texture Pattern (LDTP) and Median Ternary Pattern (MTP) descriptor characterization, followed by Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) classification. Additionally, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was trained and implemented. The results were highly satisfactory, achieving a recognition rate of 100% under a uniform background and 98.57% under a complex background.

articleTitle: FDTD Calculation of the Lightning Electromagnetic Field in Presence of a Vertically Stratified Ground and a Tall Tower: Validation and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The objective of this work was devoted to simulation of electromagnetic radiation by lightning in presence of a vertically stratified ground and a tower using an interesting numerical method, namely the FDTD-2D method. The first objective fixed was to validate the proposed approach by comparingit with measured data issued from specialized literature. After that, The electromagnetic field calculated for three soil configurations has been evaluated. The concerned ground configurations are: homogeneous and non-homogeneous soil (vertical stratified soil). According to the obtained results we can notice that FDTD approach gives an accurate results of the lightning electromagnetic field, which can be used to study The coupling between lightning's electromagnetic field and various electric, electronic, and telecommunication systems

articleTitle: A Theoretical and Experimental Investigation of Multi-Layer Composite Materials' Shielding Effectiveness Using a DTEM Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness of composite materials using the dual transverse electromagnetic cell (DTEM). To validate this method, we employed both numerical simulation and experimental measurement techniques. Specifically, we used Ansys HFSS to perform numerical simulations of the DTEM cell, and we conducted experimental measurements on a sample synthesized within the frequency range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 MHz$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 GHz$</tex>. In the experimental measurement, the test samples were introduced into the cross-section of the cell using various instruments associated with the DTEM cell. In both the experimental and numerical methods, we determined the shielding effectiveness of the samples under study in the frequency range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 MHz$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 GHz$</tex>, and compared our results with analytical predictions. Overall, our study successfully demonstrated the effectiveness of the DTEM method for analyzing the shielding properties of composite materials. These findings will have important implications for future studies of electromagnetic compatibility in related fields.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Studies for Hydrogen Production Using Spray Pyrolysis-Synthesized ZnO Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This work presents the bio-synthesis of ZnO nanostructures using lemon leaf extract for water splitting application. The objective of this work is to study and characterize ZnO samples synthesized via green synthesis, specifically using lemon extract, deposited on copper substrates by the pyrolysis spray growth process. The nanostructures bio-synthesis pathway was optimized based on the AFM (atomic force microscope) characterization technique. Photoelectrochemical studies were conducted to evaluate their performance in hydrogen production through water splitting. The results show an effective electro- chemical activity towards oxidation-reduction reactions, with an improvement of the anode and cathode peak currents with the increase of the scanning speed. Light illumination has been found to slightly decrease the electron transfer resistance of ZnO nanostructures by promoting the generation of electron- hole pairs. In addition, light exposure led to a significant increase in current, illustrating the creation of additional light-induced electron-hole pairs. These results highlight the potential of ZnO nanostructures synthesized for use in sensitive electrochemical applications. Thus, this material is very promising for hydrogen generation by water splitting.

articleTitle: Improvement Analysis of Multi-Source Knowledge-Based CFARD in Weibull Scenario and Hardware Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this work, we present a Constant False Alarm Rate Detector (CFARD), that employs a Multi-Source Knowledge (MSK) to improve Log-t CFARD performance in a non-homogenous Weibull environment. The presented MSK- CFARD combines the information extracted from the Geographic Information System (GIS) to form the Static Environmental Knowledge Base (SEKB), and the use of radar echoes to generate the Dynamic Environmental Knowledge Base (DEKB) using the Homogeneous Reference Cells Selector (HRCS). The incorporation of the MSK-CFARD in the Log-t CFARD provides an enhanced detection probability with a smaller variation in false alarm probability in non-homogeneous environments compared to existing knowledge-based detectors. Furthermore, KB-CFARDs are implemented on Advanced Digital Signal Processor (ADSP) board, and real-time constraints are discussed to satisfy real-time processing for Air Surveillance Radar ASR-12 radar.

articleTitle: A New Robust Synergetic Sliding Mode Approach Based on the Lyapunov Theorem for MPPT Controller of Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In order to ensure system stability and optimal energy efficiency, it is crucial to determinate the optimal rotational speed suited accommodates the instantaneous variations in wind speeds. This paper introduces a new approach for the wind turbine (WT) maximum power point tracking controller (MPPT), which combines the Lyapunov theorem with the synergetic sliding mode control (SSMC) to maximizing power extraction from wind speeds while ensuring system stability control under rondom operating conditions imposed by parameter and wind speed variation. Two simulation scenarios under two different wind speed density are to assess the effectiveness of this proposed strategy, comprehensive analyses are conducted comparing with conventional sliding mode control (SMC). The results indicate the robustness and superior the proposed approache performance.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Thermal Aging on the Conduction Processes in the Vegetable Oil Impregnated Kraft Paper Based Insulation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper discusses a problem linked to the formation of space charges and their transport mechanisms in power equipment's insulating systems. To meet environmental requirements, this issue is examined in a Kraft paper insulating material after being impregnated with biodegradable vegetable oil. The impregnated paper samples are examined using the polarization and depolarization Currents (PDC) technique in two distinct situations: without the effect of thermal aging and after being continuously aged for 150 hours at a temperature of 80°C. PDC measurements are carried out for three different applied electric fields: 30, 45, and 60 kV/cm. The results obtained predict good compatibility between the Kraft paper and the biodegradable oil used, relative to thermal stress, since the recorded currents in the aged samples are significantly lower than those recorded in the non-aged ones. Additionally, the polarization currents indicate the occurrence of a space charge process (currents peak feature) in the non-aged samples. The thermal aging effect is evident in the depolarization currents, with a negative relaxation current observed for the non-aged samples and a tendency toward a de-trapping process as the applied electric field is intensified in the aged impregnated paper

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Heat Controller for Domestic Appliances
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this works we present a methodology for temperature control for domestic appliances using classical Proportional-Integral (PI) and Deep learning (DL) controller. The dataset collected from the PI controller in terms of temperature error and chopper control parameters are used for training to generate a predict model that has more advantages in fulfilling the heat regulation when subject to various disturbances that are likely to occur, otherwise difficult to adjust in the PI classical parameters even with on line tuning. To consolidate and support this finding, the deep learning controller are implemented in simulation and compared to classical controller. In addition, the experimental PI results, as dataset are being exploited to elaborate a predict model well suited for implementation. In fact, it shows that the DL controller outperforms the conventional PI in terms of resilience and time response with minimal overshoot without coefficient tuning, even for other disturbances not accounted for.

articleTitle: Assessment of Waste Heat Potential of a Gas Turbine and Flare Gas System for Combined Cooling and Electricity Production
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The significant increase in energy demand conjugated with the declining capacity for fossil fuel production has led to the development of polygeneration technologies (integrated simultaneous generation of electricity, cooling and heating and other energy outputs). Such technologies are projected to enhance the energy efficiency and decrease greenhouse gas emissions, particularly for industries with high carbon footprints such as the petroleum sector. The present study investigates a Combined Cooling and Power system (CCP) energy system designed for cooling, and power generation by recovering the waste heat of a combined gas turbine and flare gas system of an Algerian upstream petroleum facility. The proposed system aims to integrate an Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) combined with an Absorption Refrigeration Cycle (ARC) to produce useful power and cooling, respectively. The energy analysis of the CCP system is implemented with the Aspen Hysys tool. The overall efficiency is improved passing from 34.6% from the basic configuration to 42.3% for the proposed new CCP configuration. This enhancement is expected to directly reduce natural gas demand and greenhouse gas emissions.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Coupled MPTCP Congestion Control Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Multipath TCP (MPTCP) has emerged as a promising protocol for enhancing network performance by utilizing multiple paths simultaneously. In this paper, we focus on measuring the performance of coupled MPTCP congestion control(CC) algorithms, specifically throughput, in the context of delay, loss rate, and bandwidth. We are going to evaluate the main coupled MPTCP congestion control algorithms: LIA, OLIA, BALIA and wVegas. The obtained results demonstrate the effectiveness of the performance analysis of different CC algorithms doing under the same plateform. Our research aims to shed light on the effectiveness of these algorithms under varying network conditions and to provide valuable insights into their suitability for different scenarios.

articleTitle: CMOS On-Chip Integrated Transformers Comparison
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper describes the comparison of two different integrated transformer topologies operating for high frequency applications. Planar stacked octagonal and circular coil topologies are studied to illustrate the good performance. The primary and secondary coils have the same dimensions with 1:1 turn ratio. The simplified physical equivalent circuit is demonstrated to evaluate its components values. Finite element method analysis was carried out to show the electromagnetic and thermal behaviour. Simulations show quality factor improvements for the flipped circular topology. The octagonal topology avoids to concentrates the current density in the angles but allows to increase the temperature due to the great number of segments. The results revealed that the planar transformer with the circular topology offers high performances.

articleTitle: An Integrated Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithm for Parameter Estimation and Maximum Power Point Tracking in Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm subjected the PV parameters to changes under faulty and weather operations conditions during runtime, which influenced the results obtained. The aim of this research is to provide an interconnected algorithm for online optimization of PV parameters. The MPPT algorithm will dynamically adjust its operations, ensuring continual optimization in response to each update of PV parameters. We choose a custom block over other simulation techniques to allow parameter updating and provide more flexibility and customization options. This paper proposes a combined meta-heuristic algorithm based on multi-objective optimization for both parameter estimation and MPPT. The simulation results under different algorithms show the efficacy of this combination in online optimization and the capability of its implementation in the real-time optimization controller. The paper also discusses the results of simulations using different candidate algorithms. Finally, this paper recommends the adaptation of this approach for multiple problems that include parameter estimation at the first level and suggests the use of advanced algorithms and techniques for the sake of accelerating time processing.

articleTitle: Current Sensor Fault Diagnosis in DFIG Wind Turbines: Kalman Filter-Based Dedicated Observer Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In wind farms, the accuracy of the measurements provided by current sensors is crucial to ensure effective monitoring and control precision. Malfunctioning of these sensors can lead to severe damages, particularly at the converter, generator, and network levels. Therefore, it is essential to quickly identify faulty sensors to ensure the proper functioning of the system, to avoid energy losses, and to reduce maintenance costs. This article presents a diagnostic method based on an array of Extended Kalman Filters (EKF), developed following the Dedicated Observer Scheme (DOS), relying on a nonlinear model of the Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG). This approach aims to estimate the rotor currents, which are then compared with sensor measurements to produce residuals used as fault indicators to detect faulty sensors. This method has been implemented on an FPGA board, and the experimental results obtained demonstrate its effectiveness, even under varying wind conditions.

articleTitle: Robustness Investigation of FOC of PMSG Based Variable-Speed Wind Turbine Connected on Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Wind energy has emerged as an increasingly viable renewable energy source, driven by rising fossil fuel costs, energy security concerns, and environmental considerations. In 2022, wind energy production grew by 9% compared to 2021, maintaining an annual rate exceeding 12% since 2012. This study focuses on the application of Field Oriented Control (FOC), a prevalent control strategy in wind power generation systems, to a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) in a variable speed wind turbine configuration. The research methodology involved implementing FOC and conducting robustness analyses through PMSG parameter variations. The primary objectives were to maximize wind energy capture efficiency while ensuring sustained control performance. MATLAB/Simulink was employed to simulate and evaluate the various components of the wind turbine system (WTS), facilitating comprehensive analysis of the results.

articleTitle: Interconnection and Damping Assignment Approach for PM Synchronous Motors, Comparison with the Classical PI Control
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Hamiltonian energy control strategy for a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) drive. The approach addresses the inherent nonlinearity of PMSM drives, which can lead to DC bus voltage instability. To enhance control performance, a state observer is incorporated for accurate load torque estimation. A comparative analysis is conducted between the proposed Hamiltonian energy control strategy and a conventional PI controller. Additionally, a flatness-based control method is employed to generate the desired current references within the nonlinear drive system. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed Hamiltonian energy control strategy in improving system performance and stability.

Author Keywords: Interconnection and damping assignment passivity based control IDA-PBC

articleTitle: Control of PUC5 Based-Grid Connected Inverter Using MPC and PI Regulator
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study presents an analysis and comparison of the MPC and PI controllers' dynamic performance. The two control structures are intended to control a single-phase PUC5 inverter that is connected to the grid via a L filter. Owing to its various benefits, the packed U-Cell converter has emerged as a potential multilevel converter architecture for a wide range of industrial applications. It achieves the maximum voltage levels with greater dependability while using fewer switch components. In order to inject a sinusoidal current with minimum THD while maintaining the capacitor voltage at its appropriate level, different control methods are employed. In this paper, two controllers are investigated the MPC and the conventional PI regulator. MATLAB/Simulink software package is used for simulation of the whole system. The results demonstrate that MPC outperforms traditional PI control in terms of tracking performance under restrictions. In other words, the MPC offers more control flexibly and better current injection into the grid with low THD.

articleTitle: Harnessing a New 5-D Hyperchaotic System with Fibonacci Q-Matrix Encryption Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Amidst the increasing demand for secure image encryption techniques, this paper presents an enhanced approach. We introduce the utilization of a 5-D hyper-chaotic system integrated into the Fibonacci Q-Matrix scheme for image encryption. The simplicity of the proposed system is evident, comprising twelve terms featuring three nonlinearities. Notably, the system demonstrates remarkable sensitivity to initial conditions, making it highly suitable for encryption purposes. To ensure the confidentiality of digital images, we employ a two-stage encryption process involving confusion and diffusion. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the hyper-chaotic system in terms of both security and performance when combined with the Fibonacci Q-Matrix scheme.

articleTitle: Traffic Sign Detection Using Multiple Cascaded Classifiers Based on LBP Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Traffic Sign Detection (TSD) is a crucial component in many applications. These include driver assistance, sign main-tenance, and the navigation of autonomous vehicles. Detection based on cascaded classifiers is a solution which has proved its efficiency. Previous work, however, have mainly considered the classical Haar and HOG descriptors as low-level characteristics. The extensive tests we conducted on the GTSDB benchmark show that LBP characteristics lead to better performances compared to the classical Haar and HOG. This comes at the expense of a higher computational burden. To improve this, further optimizations are conducted on the training parameters. We also show that the usage of three classifiers each specialized with a category of sign shapes leads to a considerable enhancement of the detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Induction Motor Diagnosis at Standstill Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The present work proposes to model the induction motor (IM) in the frequency domain to take into account the inverter association and deep bar effect with precision. The findings were verified experimentally using a three-phase IM by standstill frequency response (SSFR) approach under various failure scenarios. Time domain analysis is used to plot the IM characteristic under different broken rotor bar (BRB) numbers to verify the SSFR reliability. The model demonstrates that the suggested method is an effective instrument for IM modeling for diagnosis purposes.

articleTitle: The Degradation Evaluation of PV Modules Installed in Adrar Desert Environment by Translating STC Using the Bilinear Interpolation Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this study, we analyze the efficiency and degradation rates of photovoltaic (PV) modules exposed to desert conditions in Adrar for over 9 years. Evaluating degradation requires translating outdoor measurements to Standard Test Condition (ST-C) for comparison with manufacturer data sheets. We employ the method of linear interpolation, using four experimental I/V graphs as references, to translate measurements to STC for each PV module. We assess voltage and current characteristics through I/V and P/V curves and determine the degradation rates of various gains (Vmp, Imp, Voc, Isc, Pmax, FF) at ST-C for three PV modules: Isofoton-75W, Isofoton-100W, and Photowatt PW500, exposed to extreme desert weather conditions.

articleTitle: Real-Time FPGA Implementation of a 90° Phase Shifter Based on Hilbert Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to design an efficient architecture for FPGA real-time implementation of hilbert transform (HT) using an approach based on the half-band Finite impulse response (FIR) filter. After the creation of HT's IP-core using Vivado-HLS it has been experimentally tested with Nexys video FPGA board using a real-signals. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed system, both hardware and software implementations have been validated using Vivado and Matlab tools, respectivelly. A cosine signal generated by Analog Discovery 2 and acquired ElectroCardioGram (ECG) signal using AD8232 module have been used as inputs allowing to shift the phase of each signal by an angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> in real-time, thus forming the imaginary part of the corresponding analytical signals. The obtained results are very promising as they guarantee a very short computing time with a minimal power and resources consumption.

articleTitle: Analysis of PD for Composite Insulator with and without Pollution Using PSD Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Partial discharges (PD) represent critical precursors to insulation breakdown in high-voltage electrical systems. However, the presence of pollution can significantly affect PD characteristics, complicating detection and analysis. This study explores the power spectral density technique (PSD) to investigate the influence of pollution on PD in composite insulator exposed to High Voltage Direct Current HVDC. The composite insulator behavior (with and without pollution) has been studied by measuring leakage current and voltage. PD data were collected and analyzed using PSD. The results revealed distinct spectral features of PD in polluted insulator, highlighting specific peaks appearing in PSD signals of frequency between 25.84 and 29.54 MHZ for voltage signal, and between 25 and 90 MHz for currents. Leveraging PSD in PD monitoring programs facilitates early detection of insulation issues in real time environments.

articleTitle: Decarbonization of Gas Turbine Using Cocnentrating Solar Tower in Algeria :Cas Study
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The solar gas turbine is a power generation system that merges gas turbine technology with solar energy. Solar field utilizes mirrors or lenses to focus sunlight, producing heat used to warm air or another working fluid. This heat transfer fluid typically air or gas, is then routed to a gas turbine. The concentrated solar heat elevates the temperature and pressure, making it expand and move through the turbine, thereby generating electricity. By reducing the consumption of fossil fuels, solar gas turbines help in mitigating air pollution and the impact on climate change. Solar gas turbines are especially beneficial in sunny areas, and can be incorporated into hybrid systems that combine solar energy with fossil fuels, ensuring a stable and continuous energy supply. The objective of this work is to predict and analyze the solar hybridization of a gas turbine situated in the region of Bechar using TRNSYS code. The obtained results show that the operation of this type of power plant allows us to reduce the use of fossil sources, with a reduction in consumption reaching up to 70%, and the solar field contributes to producing about 54 MWe during the day, improving energy performance, and benefiting from an environmental perspective (reduction of CO2 propagated by gas turbines).

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of a Four-Leg Two-Level SAPF Versus a Four-Leg Three-Cell FCI-Based SAPF
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This research presents two variants of four-leg shunt active power filters: a two-level filter and a variant incorporating a Flying Capacitor Inverter (FCI). A comparative analysis is needed to demonstrate each type's efficiency and robust flexibility. The system is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink, and the simulation results affirm the effectiveness of the flying capacitor configuration. The proposed technology offers excellent robustness, strong dynamics, and high precision. The total harmonic distortion (THD) of the supply current for all algorithms remains well below the limits specified by the IEEE-519 standard. There is also a significant reduction in neutral current.

articleTitle: Image-Based Ball Tracking Using a Holonomic Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper introduces an effective ball-tracking approach employing a holonomic mobile robot. Computer vision techniques are leveraged to dynamically locate and track a moving ball within its environment. Image data is processed in real-time to extract key features of the ball, including its position and trajectory. Subsequently, Lyapunov stability analysis is utilized to ensure the convergence and stability of the tracking process.

articleTitle: Development of a Linear Motor Separator for Recovering Copper Particles of Various Sizes
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This article discusses the design and implementation of an eddy current separator prototype for the linear separation of non-ferromagnetic conductive particles. Utilizing the phenomenon of electromagnetic linear induction, the device sorts particles based on their electrical conductivity. The prototype's characteristics and performance were experimentally evaluated, demonstrating effective particle separation based on conductivity. This separator shows significant potential for various industrial applications that require precise separation of non-ferromagnetic conductive particles.

articleTitle: 5G MCM Based NOMA in Vehicular Environments: A Comparative Analysis of F-OFDM and W-OFDM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The rigorous demands of 5G communication systems, notably in Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA)-based vehicular communication scenarios, emphasize the limits of conventional Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiplexing (OFDM). The current investigation explores the performance of advanced waveforms, namely Filtered-OFDM (F-OFDM) and Windowed-OFDM (W-OFDM), as potential solutions to the challenges faced by OFDM in 5G. To compare the performance of these waveforms to standard OFDM, we evaluate the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) for various velocities and power allocation factors. The investigation shows that F-OFDM and W-OFDM perform better, particularly under high-velocity settings, because of their capacity to minimize different interferences in moderate Doubly Selective (DS) channels. This study reveals that F-OFDM and W-OFDM are outstanding options for vehicular networks operating under 5G's demanding conditions.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Hardware Architecture for Real-Time Time-Frequency Analysis: Applying STFT for the Segmentation of Non-Stationary Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The majority of physical signals that are of interest to processing tasks are of non-stationary type, and since the Fourier transform (FT) cannot give enough details on Time-frequency domain, the short-time fourier transform (STFT) was developed and has remained one of the most classic signal analysis method where many sophisticated algorithms have been created based on its modification. In this paper, HW/SW co-design technique is used to implement the STFT targeting Nexys Video FPGA board. The proposed architecture can work with a clock sampling rate up to 106 MHz to ensure a very less computation time with minimum power and resources consumption. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed system, the analysis of both real non-stationary signal generated by Analog Discovery 2 and acquired Electro-Cardio-Gram (ECG) signal using AD8232 module is validated. A comparative study has been performed with some similar related works. The proposed system represents an appropriate approach that enables us to achieve the best performances in terms of real-time, flexibility and rapidity of time-frequency analysis with the ability to intervene at all levels of the development process.

articleTitle: Elliptic-Curve Digital-Signature System Based on Radix-2w Arithmetic
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) is a widely recognized cryptographic tool that plays a crucial role in verifying the authenticity and preserving the integrity of digital messages. What distinguishes ECDSA from its peers is its exceptional ability to provide robust security with smaller key sizes, making it highly efficient, particularly in resource-constrained applications. Based on the flexibility of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Radix-2}^w$</tex> arithmetic, we propose new simple methods to ECDSA implementation handling efficiently the intricacies of elliptic curve point multiplication (PM) and double point multiplication (DPM) operations. The implementation incorporates a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Radix-2}^w$</tex> method for PM and a simultaneous <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Radix-2}^{2}$</tex> method for DPM. Both methods are streamlined one-pass recode/evaluation processes. These methods reduce the number of point additions (ADDs) to a near-optimal limit in a sublinear computational time without increasing the number of point doublings (DBLs). They also have the advantage to require a minimal number of point-precomputations. In addition, they show high resilience against side-channel attacks. In comparison to the standard binary method used in PM and DPM, the new <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Radix-2}^w$</tex> methods shows substantial savings in computational time.

articleTitle: Design of Sliding Mode Observer -Controller for Stick-Slip Vibration Suppression in Drill String Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The primary cause of the Stick-slip phenomenon, torsional vibrations, has a major impact on drilling operations and poses a serious risk to drilling efficiency and equipment integrity. Stick-slip-induced vibrations have the potential to seriously harm drilling equipment if they are not controlled, which emphasizes the critical need for automated, real-time management techniques. The main goal of this research is to develop and put into practice a cascaded method that can reduce these vibrations in a real-time, closed-loop system. The paper's main goal is to accomplish this by integrating a sliding mode observer and controller and taking advantage of their versatility and robustness to successfully reduce torsional vibrations during drilling operations. The study aims to prove the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed cascaded technique in real-world drilling scenarios through simulation-based experimentation and analysis. Through the application of sophisticated control techniques to the Stick-slip phenomenon, this research aims to improve drilling efficiency, increase equipment longevity, and ultimately optimize drilling operations in difficult environments.

articleTitle: Circulating Current Suppressing in Two Parallel-Connected Inverters Supplied a Water Pump Drive Using a Non-Linear Control Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a strategy for suppressing high-frequency circulating current components for parallel-connected inverters. Traditionally, the interleaving method results in a higher circulating current flowing through two-level voltage source inverters. Coupling inductors are used only to minimize circulating currents of low-frequency components, but not the high frequency. When these circulating currents increase significantly, it can lead to saturation of the coupling inductances, increased switching losses, and decreased overall system performance. This article introduces a new control method based on a sliding mode controller (SMC) for parallel-connected inverters powering an induction machine used as a water pump. This controller reduces the value of the high-frequency components of the zero-sequence circulating current (ZSCC). Experimental results validate the effectiveness and performance of the proposed modulation and control strategy.

articleTitle: Indoor Localization for Epileptic Patients Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Epilepsy is a disease that can cause dangerous accidents, especially in certain circumstances, such as when the patient is climbing stairs. For this reason, it is important to predict seizures and provide permanent assistance to the patient. As the epileptic patient is often lonely, an autonomous assistive device can be a lifesaver. In this paper, we propose a device that can predict seizures and inform medical staff about the patient's location. In indoor environments, the global positioning system is a low-accuracy localization technology. This limitation is tackled by presenting an indoor localization based inertial measurement unit. In addition, a method for detecting falling is proposed to rescue the patient, particularly if he is alone in a large building. The proposed localization technique achieves a precision of 34 cm, while the proposed help device has an effectiveness of 98.5%.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Deep Neural Network Architecture RefineUnet for Ultrasound Thyroid Nodules Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Thyroid nodules are prevalent in the human population, often identified during routine ultrasound examinations. Accurate segmentation of these nodules is crucial for diagnosing and managing potential thyroid malignancies. However, precise segmentation of the complex thyroid tissue remains challenging due to the ultrasound image's low contrast and high noise. Several traditional segmentation approaches to detect thyroid nodules suffer from imprecise localization issues, while deep learning techniques offer promising solutions. This study proposes a new deep hybrid architecture that combines the encoder-decoder structure of U-Net with the multi-resolution RefineNet modules to improve the model's ability to recognize thyroid nodules. The proposed approach demonstrates the impact of combining residual blocks and chained residual pooling (CRP) blocks to effectively capture both local detail and global context, resulting in robust semantic segmentation. This is particularly important in thyroid nodule segmentation, where accurate diagnosis and treatment planning require both fine-scale features and contextual information. The model was trained and verified using the public TN3K dataset, which consists of 3493 thyroid nodule images. Our approach was found to significantly improve the accuracy of semantic segmentation, achieving 94.18% with an IOU of 96.40% compared to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Real Time Face Recognition System using Raspberry Pi4
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Modern technologies like computer vision (CV), Artificial Intelligence (AI), the internet of things (IoT), and (AIoT) Artificial Intelligence of Things have advanced in many fields, particularly surveillance systems, which need to process faces in real time to guarantee security. This paper proposed a comparative analysis for a real time face recognition system from video sequences with two architectures including traditional application using a personal computer and a Raspberry Pi, respectively. Our study offers an implementation for a real-time face recognition system employing Viola-Jones algorithm and Deep neural networks techniques such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for face detection and face recognition. Our face recognition system seeks to replace the conventional approach of keeping track of attendance by implementing a Raspberry Pi-based attendance monitoring system that can be utilized by all institutions and organizations. Significant progress has been made thanks to the use of CNN models which has allowed an accuracy rate of 94%.
