articleTitle: Refined Approach for Rain Cloud Motion Estimation Using the Center of Mass Forecasting Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Today, meteorologists are increasingly interested in cloud tracking and forecasting their future positions. This capability is crucial for identifying rainy regions and predicting potential weather-related catastrophes in advance. Our contribution aims to test several tracking methods on radar images that were initially developed for satellite imagery. The first step of our approach involves filtering out undesirable echoes from the image, followed by isolating each cloud cell. The displacement of the clouds is represented by their Center of Mass Motion (COM), which serves as a reference for evaluating the results. We estimate the COM using various algorithms, specifically the Difference Based Approach (DBA), Mean Path Adjustment (MPA), and Adjusted Mean Path Adjustment (AMPA). The efficiency of these algorithms is evaluated based on error estimation, and the findings indicate promising results.

articleTitle: Optimizing Grid-Connected Microgrid Energy Management Through Advanced Heuristic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In response to the urgent need for renewable energy development and variability management due to escalating population growth, rising energy demands, and diminishing natural reserves, this research focuses on optimizing energy management within a grid-connected microgrid. The study uniquely employs advanced heuristic algorithms to define system choices and constraints, achieving significant improvements in energy efficiency and cost reduction. Utilizing Matlab Simulink and Stateflow environments, various simulation scenarios are explored to demonstrate the benefits of the proposed approach, including enhanced stability and reliability of the energy supply. The findings highlight the potential for significant advancements in microgrid energy management through innovative algorithmic strategies.

articleTitle: RTLAB-Based Performance Validation of PV- Powered Single-Phase Asynchronous Motor Pumps
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this paper, a comprehensive investigation of the performance evaluation and validation of a single-phase asynchronous motor pump system coupled with a photovoltaic (PV) power source is presented. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the practicality and effectiveness of this configuration for pumping applications. The RTLAB platform, which enables real-time simulation and emulation of dynamic systems, includes important components, such as the use of a single-phase asynchronous motor as the pump's power source, the incorporation of a PV system to supply renewable energy, and the use of RTLAB for real-time validation. Through rigorous simulation and experimentation, the motor response performance, such as speed, torque, and current response, was analyzed under varying solar irradiance and load conditions. In addition, the PV power and DC bus voltage were supervised after motor driving. This research fills the knowledge gap between the theoretical analysis and real-world applications of single-phase asynchronous motor pump systems combined with PV sources. This approach, which validates the results using RTLAB, provides a validation method to evaluate the performance and guide design choices for effective and environmentally friendly pumping solutions. Keywords- Single-phase asynchronous motors, PV, RTLAB validation, SimPower System MATLAB.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Optimization Using FEM-GA Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges associated with designing high-performance wireless power transfer (WPT) systems for various applications. The efficient operation of WPT systems is crucial, but it must meet specific restrictions imposed by the application. This is particularly true for WPT systems used in biomedical implants, sensor applications, and IoT devices, where a small receiving coil is required while maintaining high power transfer efficiency (PTE). The PTE is dependent on several design parameters, such as coil design, coil size, relative geometry, operating frequency, and load. Our paper begins by defining the finite element method and details the parametric-coil modeling in Ansys Maxwell. We then propose the optimization of the wireless power transfer efficiency via the FEM-GA. Furthermore, the suggested WPT coil design method improves the transfer efficiency by a maximum of 74%. Ultimately, we verify the accuracy of our findings by employing finite element simulation with Simplorer.

articleTitle: Prediction of the Photovoltaic Behavior of In0.3Ga0.7N PIN Solar Cell VIA Intrinsic Layer Doping Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this paper we present an optimization analysis of the doping of the intrinsic layer of an In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>N PIN solar cell conducted experimentally. This analytical approach aims to determine the optimal doping value for the intrinsic layer, which may not always be experimentally determined in certain cases. Subsequently, this determined value will be utilized in calculating the output parameters, particularly focusing on enhancing the conversion efficiency of the solar cell. To comprehensively evaluate the photovoltaic characteristics of the In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>N PIN homojunction solar cell, we used numerical simulation with PC1D software. This simulation aims to ensure the achievement of both short-circuit current, open-circuit-voltage and high conversion efficiency. Specifically, we have simulated the current-voltage (I-V) characteristic of this cell under AM1.5G solar illumination conditions, just as we also simulated the quantum efficiency (QE) curve. The influence of carrier lifetime and front surface recombination velocity on photovoltaic quantities has been investigated.

articleTitle: Enhancing MPPT Efficiency in Standalone Photovoltaic Systems: Integration of Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control with Optimized Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control (FSC-MPC) strategy tailored for optimizing Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) in standalone photovoltaic systems. Leveraging a dynamic model of a boost converter, the FSC-MPC strategy integrates a unique cost function, which incorporates the absolute difference between the reference and predicted current to effectively regulate the boost switch, thereby enhancing reference tracking and minimizing losses. An advancement in this strategy involves the inclusion of an additional term in the cost function aimed at optimizing the switching frequency, thus reducing losses and attenuating undesirable oscillations. The FSC-MPC's current reference generation relies on an optimized Artificial Neural Network (OP-ANN) architecture, wherein parameters such as the number of hidden layers, neurons per layer, and activation function are dynamically adjusted using a pattern-search algorithm (PSA). By minimizing the loss function through adjusting these parameters, the optimization algorithm ensures more effective learning and enhances the ANN's adaptability to changing environmental conditions. The proposed model is implemented, modeled, and simulated within the MATLAB/Simulink environment, with extensive discussion of simulation results providing a comprehensive evaluation of the performance of the proposed algorithms.

Author Keywords: Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control

articleTitle: An Intelligent Sequential Approach for Traffic Single Agent Lights Signals Control
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Traffic congestion in cities poses challenges, waiting time and frustrating commuters. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) offers solutions by enabling agents to learn optimal strategies. This paper explores DRL's application in optimizing urban traffic light systems. Recent advancements in reinforcement learning, including deep neural networks and real-time data integration, promise intelligent adaptive traffic lights. This paper introduces a new intelligent sequential approach named SSE_DQN (Self Sequential Estimator Deep Q Network), this approach enhances learning performance by incorporating insights like optimal lane-changing and dynamic condition responses. SSE_DQN represents a significant advancement, potentially alleviating congestion and improving urban transportation efficiency. Through simulations and real-world testing, its effectiveness in adapting to traffic patterns is demonstrated. This research contributes to intelligent transportation systems, showcasing DRL's potential in addressing urban challenges.

articleTitle: Optimizing Microgrid Energy Management using Reinforcement Double Deep Q-Networks with Prioritized Experience Replay
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Driven by recent advances and applications in smart grid technologies, our electric power grid is undergoing radical modernization. Microgrids (MG) represent a transformative approach in power delivery, shifting from centralized to distributed systems with localized generation from various sources. However, this decentralization necessitates efficient energy management systems (EMS) to ensure optimal operation, stability, and integration with the main grid. Additionally, using energy storage helps provide electrical energy savings and independence from the local utility. Focusing on storage system management, this paper proposes an advanced approach using a reinforcement learning agent based on Double Deep Q-Networks (DDQN) with Prioritized Experience Replay for storage system management within a microgrid. Unlike traditional model-based approaches that fall short when managing the dynamic nature of microgrids, the proposed solution builds a robust agent tasked with managing the charging and discharging of batteries, taking into account the dynamic interactions of various energy sources and demand. This approach aims to maintain the battery state of charge (SoC) within a healthy range, optimize resource utilization, and ensure continuous power supply. A simulated microgrid environment, developed using Simulink and Python, serves as the testbed for evaluating and demonstrating the agent's effectiveness across various energy management scenarios.

articleTitle: Optimizing Wavelength Division Multiplexing Free-Space Optical Systems: A Comparative Analysis of Predictive Modeling Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of telecommunications, Free-Space Optical (FSO) communication systems are increasingly positioned as promising candidates for next-generation networks. Their immunity to interference and high bandwidth perfectly align with the surging demand for high-speed data transmission. This research dives deep into the world of cutting edge predictive modeling techniques, which are essential for optimizing Wavelength Division Multiplexing FSO systems and addressing fading effects in atmospheric conditions. To rigorously assess the predictive power of various models, we utilize cutting edge OptiSystem simulations. Four Machine Learning (ML) models, including Fine Trees, linear Support Vector Machines (SVMs), boosted trees, and linear regression models incorporating interaction terms, are evaluated to identify the most effective model for accurate performance prediction of the WDM- FSO system, specifically in terms of key metrics like Q-Factor, Signal- to Noise Ratio (SNR) and Bit Error Rate (BER). A comprehensive approach is employed. Extensive data is generated through meticulous simulations of a wide range of atmospheric conditions. Further, leveraging rigorous evaluation techniques like Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), R-squared, Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE), an in depth comparison of the four aforementioned algorithms is performed. This thorough analysis provides valuable insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each model, ultimately guiding the selection of the optimal model for next-generation WDM-FSO systems.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Feasibility Study of Developing Wind Turbines in Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study explores the potential of onshore wind energy in Algeria amid global efforts to combat climate change through renewable energy adoption. The research proposes the bimodal mixture Weibull distribution for wind speed modeling and evaluates four parameter estimation methods for optimal wind speed data fitting. Economic feasibility studies highlight the viability of wind energy projects, with competitive electricity costs compared to standard tariffs. Notably, In-Salah emerges as the most favorable site for wind energy generation, characterized by high capacity factor, superior benefit cost ratios, and short payback periods. Sidi-Bel-Abbas, despite its low classification, proves more feasible to wind energy than Chlef and El-Oued. With H25.0-60kW turbine deployment, Sidi-Bel-Abbas can achieve a 38% capacity factor, generate 202 GWh annually at 3.81 c$/kWh with an 8-year payback period.

articleTitle: Advancing Echo Processing Techniques by Combining Support Vector Machine and Weber's Law Integration *
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Removing ground echoes from weather radar images is crucial for data accuracy. We propose advanced methods using Weber's Law Descriptors (WLD) and Weber's Law with Local Binary Pattern (WLBP) descriptors, combined with Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers, to differentiate ground echoes from precipitation. Testing at the Setif and Bordeaux sites showed that these techniques effectively eliminate ground echoes while preserving precipitation. Our methods offer several advantages over traditional techniques, including enhanced local contrast sensitivity and improved texture analysis, leading to higher classification accuracy. Cross-validation confirmed the robustness and generalizability of our approach across different weather conditions and radar systems, suggesting its potential for widespread adoption in meteorology.

articleTitle: Shielding Impact on Efficiency of Electric Wind Blower for Solar Panel Cleaning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this study, we conduct a numerical analysis to investigate the impact of shielding on the efficiency of a blower device to generate an electric wind for cleaning solar panels. The device consists of two wires and grid electrodes, with the wires exposed to high positive DC voltage while the grid and the wall remain grounded. Our investigation primarily focuses on understanding the effect of the distance between the two wires (or the shielding effect), on the conversion of the electric energy into a mechanical energy of the gas flow generated by the blower. The used numerical model is based on the calculation of electro-hydrodynamic (EHD) force generated by the corona discharge and then the resolution of the Navier-Stokes equations. Our findings reveal that smaller distance between the wires leads to a greater decrease in electric current, space charge, electro-hydrodynamic (EHD) force of the blower. In contrast, the efficiency of the blower divulges a rise. The results underscore the critical importance of considering the shielding effect in the design and the development of blower devices relying on the generation of the electro-hydrodynamic (EHD) gas flow.

articleTitle: Optimal Trajectory Planning and Robust Control for Enhanced Unmanned Ground Vehicle Performance *
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study focuses on formulating a trajectory planning approach employing the mobile robot. Our primary objective lies in ensuring stability and real-time tracking of a reference trajectory, considering dynamic stability limits and accounting for the impact of disturbances during trajectory planning. The proposed approach in this paper employs a potential field method to facilitate the robot's trajectory tracking while effectively avoiding obstacles. A series of experiments conducted under realistic conditions validate the robust performance of the technique, leveraging the QBot-2e mobile robot. The results demonstrate promising outcomes in achieving accurate trajectory tracking while effectively mitigating disturbances and ensuring obstacle avoidance.

articleTitle: Synthesis, Characterization, and Theoretical Investigation of Cadmium Sulfide Thin Films (CdS) for Biosensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper explores a detailed study of cadmium sulfide (CdS) thin films, combining experimental and theoretical approaches. These films, produced through spray pyrolysis, were carefully analyzed for their structural and morphological properties using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The optical attributes were evaluated using reflectance and transmittance measurements within the [1.5-3.5] eV interval. Theoretical insights were obtained by applying the full-potential linearized augmented plane wave (FP-LAPW) framework. The findings establish that the CdS thin films possess a polycrystalline nature with a wurtzite structure. SEM imaging indicates a smooth surface morphology, with grain sizes ranging from 480 to 930 nm. Energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) confirmed the films' high crystallinity, displaying a rough, dense texture. The semiconducting behavior of CdS, distinguished by its direct optical energy gap located at the Γ point of the Brillouin zone, is linked to charge transfer mechanisms that contribute to its ionic nature. The density of states near the band gap is significantly influenced by s-p orbital interactions. This study stands out for its comprehensive integration of both theoretical modeling and experimental analysis of CdS thin films, with a specific emphasis on their potential applications, including biosensors. It offers a unified method for exploring the bulk material and thin-film characteristics of CdS materials by integrating empirical data with theoretical insights.

articleTitle: A Novel Experimental Approach for Predictive High-Frequency Modeling of Differential-Mode Impedance in Three-Phase Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: High-frequency (HF) models of electrical motors and converters are crucial for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) characterization of electrical drives and EMI filter design. This paper presents a methodology for predictive modeling of the differential-mode (DM) impedance of a three-phase high-frequency induction motor, considering frequency-dependent parameters. The proposed modeling approach establishes an equivalent circuit for the three-phase high-frequency induction motor, facilitating analysis of the electromagnetic interference (EMI) effect of each parameter and prediction of the main path of differential mode current. Transfer functions have been tuned using an asymptotic identification method to match the behavior of real impedances of motor parameters as a function of frequency in the differential-mode configuration. Prediction results demonstrate satisfactory agreement with measurements across a wide frequency bandwidth [100 Hz-20 MHz].

articleTitle: Visual Servoing-Enhanced Optimal Control for Trajectory Tracking in 2-DOF Ball on Plate Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Addressing the intricate challenges of precise ball trajectory tracking on a 2-DOF balancing system requires innovative approaches due to the system's inherent nonlinearity and instability. This study proposes a focused examination of advanced control techniques, specifically emphasizing the application of the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) as an exemplar of optimal control strategies. We delve into crafting a robust model for the 2-DOF ball balancer, setting the stage for a comprehensive exploration of optimal control efficacy. Our investigation prioritizes the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) method, highlighting its advantages and performance metrics in comparison to Full State Feedback control. Utilizing MATLAB Simulink alongside Quarc software, integrated with Quanser's 2DOF ball balancer hardware, we rigorously evaluate the LQR's operational effectiveness. The outcomes distinctly showcase the LQR's superior capability in ensuring optimal transient and steady-state responses, significantly minimizing steady-state error to an unprecedented 0.641mm. This starkly contrasts with the Full State Feedback approach, underlining the LQR's substantial benefits in managing complex, nonlinear systems like the 2-DOF ball balancer.

articleTitle: Emitter Thickness and Solar Cell Efficiency: The Role of Deep-Level Defects and Auger Recombination
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper meticulously examines the impact of deep traps on solar cell performance, focusing on key factors including open-circuit voltage, short-circuit current density, and overall efficiency. The objective is to mitigate these adverse effects through targeted optimization of diffusion depth and doping levels in N+PP+ type solar cells. Advanced simulations using COMSOL software are employed to directly link technological design, recombination phenomena, charge carrier entrapment, and the observed characteristics and parameters. The findings highlight that while Auger recombination is a predominant source of performance disruption in solar cells, the presence of deep traps or defects significantly amplifies this degradation. Specifically, it has been observed that short-circuit current densities may experience reductions of up to 0.95%. Additionally, open-circuit voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Voc)$</tex> sees decreases in the order of 3.63%, while conversion efficiency is impacted by approximately 5.42%. Optimally, it has been demonstrated that these performance metrics can be substantially improved by - adjusting the emitter thickness to FFFFFF <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.4 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> and by intensively doping the emitter at a level of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^{20}\text{cm}^{-3}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Efficient Obstacle Avoidance and Target Tracking in Mobile Robots using Advanced Technique *
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Our study focuses on the design and implementation of an autonomous mobile robot, combining advanced computer vision techniques with a microprocessor for enhanced navigation capabilities. The primary objective is to develop a self-navigating robot that seamlessly moves from a starting point to a target while employing real-time obstacle avoidance and dynamic decision-making. By continuously scanning its environment using computer vision, the robot detects and adjusts its trajectory to avoid obstacles. Embedded algorithms enable precise obstacle identification, ensuring safe and collision-free navigation. Upon reaching the target, the robot autonomously halts. If the target is hidden, the robot explores its surroundings; if the target remains undetected, it signals its inability to achieve the goal. Powered by a Raspberry Pi, this system offers a robust and cost-effective solution for mobile robot navigation. The integration of advanced computer vision and obstacle avoidance significantly enhances the robot's operational capabilities, enabling effective navigation and target pursuit in complex environments.

articleTitle: Enhanced Trajectory Planning with Robust Interval Type 2 Fuzzy Logic Controller for Unmanned Surface Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Autonomous navigation is essential for the efficiency of Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) but current solutions struggle with real-world complexities. The Type 1 Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC-Tl) is popular but limited in handling uncertainties. The Interval Type 2 Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC-T2) offers a robust alternative. This study presents an advanced trajectory planning algorithm using FLC-T2 for USVs in variable water currents, integrating a dynamic model that accounts for wheel slipping and parameter uncertainties. Comparative analysis with the FLC- T1 controller shows FLC-T2's superior performance, particularly in challenging conditions. Employing FLC- T2 enhances USV navigation, improving autonomy and reliability.

articleTitle: Accelerating Image Processing Functions on ZYNQ-FPGA Using the Vitis Vision Library
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In the last decade, we have witnessed a high demand for high-resolution devices and screens. 4K and higher becomes a standard video definition, which requires special calculators such as DSPs, GPUs, TPUs, VPUs, and FPGAs. Among these accelerators, Xilinx has recently proposed a new system on chips -All programmable SOC, combining ARM processors and Artix-like mid-scale FPGA. Moreover, to facilitate implementation, Xilinx has upgraded their previous Vivado and Vivado HLS IDEs to the recent Vitis platform. In this work, we took advantage of these recent tools to design and implement higher-resolution image-processing applications on the PYNQ-Z1 board equipped with Zynq-7000 all-programmable SOC. We have accelerated OpenCV functions from the Vitis Vision Library by designing a processing system and programmable logic PS-PL scheme using Vitis HLS and Vivado. The co-design was ensured using the AXI interface to communicate between the PS and PL. Various image processing applications were designed and tested using Python in Jupiter Notebook. Results show that our co-design on the PYNQ-Z1 board accelerates edge detectors about 30× compared to the CPU implementation, while image filtering applications are accelerated by 10×. articleTitle: Assessing the Impact Of Time Intervals On PM2.5 Prediction Using LSTM Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Air pollution is a global issue with profound implications to human health and environmental sustainability. Especially, PM2.5, which refers to particulate matter with a size of 2.5 microns or smaller, poses significant health risks. Therefore, accurately predicting PM2.5 levels is crucial. In this aim, various machine-learning methods are employed for PM2.5 prediction. The problem arises from the use of collected datasets at varied time intervals (5 minutes, 15 minutes, 1 hour, etc.), resulting in inconsistency across predictive approaches. While shorter time intervals seems to offer heightened sensitivity to changes, implying simpler prediction, this presumption may not be universally applicable. This paper investigates the impact of time intervals on PM2.5 prediction through a comparative analysis of datasets collected at different intervals (15 minutes, 1 hour, and 8 hours) using Long Short Term Memory Neural Networks (LSTM). By leveraging statistical analysis and predictive modeling techniques, we assess the dataset's distributions and evaluate prediction model performance. This study underscores the importance of interval selection in PM2.5 prediction and informs future efforts to enhance air quality surveillance and public health protection measures.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Road Extraction from Satellite Images Using D-LinkNet34
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The extraction of roads from satellite images is crucial in remote sensing, particularly in fields such as urban planning, road map updates, and autonomous driving. This task is complex due to the small size, winding configuration, and potential obstruction of roads by building shadows, posing a challenge for deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs). Our study investigates and compares the effectiveness of the LinkNet algorithm and its combination using a semantic segmentation neural network. We propose a methodology, named D-LinkNet34, which integrates the benefits of residual learning, dilated convolution, and a pre-trained ResUnet34 encoder. This approach offers significant advantages, facilitating the training of deep networks and enabling better information propagation while reducing parameter requirements. Experiments conducted with satellite images have demonstrated the superiority of D-LinkNet34 over other models such as U-Net and LinkNet34, achieving minimal losses and superior visual results, especially in complex environments. These findings confirm the relevance of our approach for road detection in large-scale satellite images.
